title: The Original Three Countries in One Day: France, Andorra, Spain from Barcelona
description: Visit Andorra, France, and Spain in a single day on a tour from Barcelona that takes in historic architecture, gorgeous mountain landscapes, and three distinctive cultures. If your time is limited, choosing a guided tour ensures you see more than you would on your own, from breakfast in Spain to lunch in a traditional French restaurant (own expense), with a series of fascinating sightseeing stops throughout the day.

reviews.usertext:
This was a very intimate tour (we rode in a very comfortable van as a total of 7 people, which was a nice surprise. I was expecting a tour bus). The places visited were everything you would expect: a sleepy village in Spain, a ski-resort town in France, and a 'bustling' capital of one of the smallest countries in the world in Andorra. Our tour guide was very friendly and knowledgeable (although he did drive a little too fast).

As you would expect from driving up and over mountains, the roads were filled with hills and turns, so be prepared to be in the car for long stretches of time. Overall, my family and I highly enjoyed the tour, and would recommend to anyone who wants to see something unusual while in Barcelona.

Great trip. A bit long but understandable considering the mileage we covered. Each of the three stops allowed us to take in the country we visited. Jordi, our guide was very knowledgeable about each site and also gave a wealth of information en route between stops. He also was kind enough to jump off the bus and had border control at Andorra stamp each of our passports. My only complaint was the driver. Antonio, although a nice guy drove a bit fast in wet weather where the front wheels lost traction once around a curve. I understand wanting to stay on schedule but our live were in his hands, especially around the tight curvy mountain roads.

This was an absolutely lovely, interesting and surprisingly relaxing tour. I highly recommend anyone w a day to spare to enjoy this trip through the mountains to France and Andorra. Our tour guide was charming and knowledgeable and I imagine she’s going to just get better and better based on her natural ability to share her love of history/travel with her guests. Don’t miss it! Well worth the money. We saw a beautiful white wolf running up the mountain. Beautiful.

First let me say that Arnau was a great tour guide. He was very informative and great to engage with.
The reason for 3 stars was that my expectations and reality was totally different.
First we went to Baga to grab some food. We didn’t do really any exploring, just food/drink if you want it and then a quick walk around town and then back on the bus. The town was cute but nothing blew my mind away.
Next was Ax le Themes. Again, a typical small town but nothing that was amazing. I dipped my feet into the outdoor hot spring, which was the highlight of this town. We had one hour to explore/get lunch, but it was too early to get lunch (we got there at 11am to leave at 12pm). So you just walk around in a circle endlessly, as there was really nothing to look at.
Then we went to Andorra. The pull over bus stops were great and the highlight of the whole trip. Yes, the 2 quick pullover stops to look at the beautiful scenery was the highlight. Once you got to Andorra, you again had an hour, but all Andorra is, is a shopping haven. If you wanna shop for name brand clothes and luxury items then this is the place for you. But I’m not a shopper, so again o walked around aimlessly for an hour. We were told we can get food there but every restaurant had lines out the door so 1hr was not enough time to get food. Luckily I brought a sandwich on this trip so I was able to eat.
Again Arnau was great but don’t be fooled by the pics. The pics represented are mostly the bus pull over stops. If you want to shop for name brand stuff then I highly recommend this, otherwise it’s not worth it.

The trip waa going well until we had to spend an hour shopping in the main shopping area of Andorra.Andorra is quite a boring place looking somewhat like a large ski village offering duty free shopping.
Sadly on a cultural tour we were left to fill in the time in an ugly noisy shopping mall. Why would I come to Spain to do what I can do at home? The usual shops selling shoes dresses shirts etc. Why mix visiting beautiful villages with a shopping mall?
We finally left and headed back to Barcelona. The traffic was almost at a stand still so our guide who had been quite ok was also very tired. The whole group was tired. She decided to talk all the time on the way home. What we needed was peace and quite but she was on a roll with a microphone that was cutting in and out. Then just to add to the commotion she linked her mobile phone to the microphone and Freddy Mercury was belting out Barcelona at about 90 decibels.
I asked if this was necessary and the guide’s response was it was compulsory. The punters obviously needed to be reeved up before leaving the bus.
The final last straw was delivering us to a location away from the original pick up point . This was not something I had been alerted to and I had no map with me. I eventually walked 6 blocks and through many wrong paths in the Gothic area when I was dead tired and arrived at my hotel at 7.30 pm having started at 6.30 am
I wouldn’t have been so tired but for the shopping mall ‘experience’ which I could well have foregone
The first thing I did on returning to my hotel was to cancel a future day trip as I didn’t want another episode like that one.

We had anticipated this being a long day and had prepared for this.

The stops in Baga, France & Andorra we’re all welcome as it’s nice to stretch your legs even if only for a short time.

Our guide Rod was a pleasant and knowledgeable man, who knew a lot about the area and was only too happy to answer any questions.

What turned the day sour for me was when we stopped on the way back. I was asked what I would like to drink, water, coffee or wine by the guide, I replied coffee and proceeded to go to the loo.

I was not made aware these drinks was bought for us at anytime and the booking states that food and drinks are not included.

I returned to the group and was invited to collect my coffee, i did so and proceeded to quickly move away from the group as I was smoking.

At this point the guide Rod, made a sarcastic comment “thank you” whilst my back was turned, and to the whole group standing around.

I returned to Rod and offered to pay for the drinks immediately (a tea and coffee for myself and my partner) as I thought we were going to be billed anyway to be refused and informed they had paid.

Please don’t make sarcastic comments behind your guest’s back, I didn’t know that Rod paid for the drinks as I was at the loo whilst they were brought out.

I left a €10 tip, but please take this as payment for the tea & coffee, not for what was a brilliant day slightly spoiled by ones attempts to embarrass a paying customer.

It is a long day and a long drive, especially for the guides, maybe too long and tiring towards the end.

The actual tour was wonderful. The guide was excellent and the cities in the 3 countries were fabulous to see and experience. BUT!!! The bus that was used was way too small for the number of people on the tour. Every seat on the small bus was occupied. We (4 of us) unfortunately got the back of the bus. There were 4 seats that should accommodate children only. We spent the entire 12 hour tour switching as to who could sit with their shoulders facing forward. One person had to sit sideways the entire trip. It was not comfortable at all and was also unsafe when we went around the sharp turns in the mountains. We couldn't wait to get off of the bus at each scheduled stop. We couldn't ask anyone else (all strangers) to switch with us, because it wouldn't be fair to them. This bus seat situation spoiled the entire tour.
There were 2 busses on this tour. The other bus was much bigger. unfortunately for us, we got the small bus.
I am not sure how you can satisfy us now, other than refund some of our ticket cost.
Please reply to this review at my email, if possible.
For anyone booking this tour in the future, please check the size of the bus compared to the number of people who are getting on. You don't want to be in the last 4 seats!!

We were very excited about this trip and knew what to expect after reading all the reviews online and the itinerary.

It was an early start, we met at 7am at the offices. The offices were a bit hard to find but we found them just in time. The offices are a five minute walk away from the nearest metro.

There were a few problems when we got at the offices behind the scenes but they were quickly resolved and we set off about 10-15 minutes later. The coach was comfortable, with spacious seats and it was air conditioned. Our guide was Giordi (George).

It took about 1.5 hours to reach Baga. We hopped off the coach and were shown where to grab a coffee and a pastry and then given about a half hour tour of the small town. Baga was a gorgeous small town. Due to time limitations we could only explore a small part of the town.

We next drove to France, 1.5 hours away, the scenery was beautiful and it did not seem that long a journey. Once we got to France, we were show where to dip our feet in the thermal springs. We remembered to pack a small towel to dry our feet off. We did not have an opportunity to explore which was a shame as there was just about enough time for lunch. We were there for about 1.5 hours.

We then drove to Andorra which is the part we were most excited about. The roads were rather windy and I felt quite sick most of this part. We got to the border and jumped out to get a picture taken. We also got our passports stamped. We then went to the capital city and spent about an hour wandering around the shopping centre. I would rather have explored the rural parts of the country rather than having to spend all the time in a shopping centre. This was a big letdown.

The journey back was directly back to Barcelona with one restroom break. We were dropped off nearby the offices where we had met in the morning.

To make the most of your time there, I would take some snacks and drinks with you so you don't spend all your time in the various countries waiting for a meal. Pack a towel for France so you can dry your feet, prepare to get travel sick as the roads are windy in Andorra, have a plan of what you would like to see in the towns so you maximise your time there and lastly, take something to read/listen to on the coach to pass the time. The tour guide didn't speak all the time so it was nice to have the quiet times to have a snooze. All in all I would recommend this tour as long as you are fully aware that what you will see at each country is rather limited.

My husband and I have traveled the world and taken dozens of tours. This tour ranks right up there as one of the WORST. We realized when we booked that this 12 hour day would mostly be a bus ride. “Ray”, our guide, was a nice enough young man, but a terrible tour guide. We learned more about Andorra and our surroundings on Google as we made our way from Barcelona to our final destination. There was little or no commentary. As we boarded the bus we were told that a mask was mandatory. Ray did not enforce that rule. I have to add that Ray was also very difficult to understand. To top it off, a toddler, sitting behind us with her parents whined and cried for 12 hours straight. It’s one thing to have children on a 12 hour tour and a totally different ball game to have a toddler.

This was an amazing adventure! Going to Andorra alone was a once in a lifetime experience for us. It's such a small country that we wouldn't end up there unless in Barcelona. The price of this tour is very affordable considering the beautiful bus we took and our guide being so knowledgeable and friendly. Luda (not sure if I spelled her name right) was a wonderful guide!

Fully mentally prepared for the long bus ride; ended up really enjoying the beautiful scenery along the way.

I loved the Andorra visit as well. Some reviews said they didn't really the shopping in the capital city. Well, I didn't really shop but I really liked my walk anyways. It is strange and yet great to see bustling streets with mountain ranges as backdrop.

I didn't really like the stops in Bagá (Spain) and Ax-Les-Thermes (France). While it was always nice to see villages, I kinda found them "meh". It felt like these stops are just out of convenience and for the sake of meeting the "3 countries" advertisement. I feel that there may be cooler places to visit along the route.

Our guide Steven and driver "Angel" were great though and as there were 2 groups traveling together, we had a much bigger bus which turned out to be much better than the mini buses!

I booked this tour back in April 2018. The experience was well worth the lengthy travel time with the highlight being Andorra (please note that most if not all international mobile phone plans do not include Andorra and usage in this particular country has been known to be quite expensive). With a variety of stops on the itinerary, the pace of the tour was surprisingly great as I never felt rushed. I had plenty of time to take a variety of Instagram-worthy pictures at every stop. The professionalism and knowledge of our tour guide was greatly appreciated.

Very nice three countries in one day tour. Martha was a good tour guide, although sometimes her sense of humor was so deadpan, we thought she was serious when she was actually joking. I had a lot of fun on the trip, but there were a few things to be aware of. The bus seats are narrow, you cannot sit two large people together, luckily my travel companion was able to sit in his own double seat as was I, but if the bus is crowded you won't be able to do that. When arriving in France, we got there long before most of the restaurants opened for lunch at noon and we only had approximately an hour to eat, luckily there was one restaurant that opened at 11:30 so we could go there, but it was so crowded we were late to the bus anyway. We didn't have time to buy souvenirs in France. Also buying at the bakery and drinking coffee in the cafe was crowded and rushed. More time there would have been much appreciated.

Large bus with 23 guest. Tour ran late bad traffic. Started 7am finished 930 pm. So spent 9 hrs on bus nice views, although 2hrs was dark in stop and go very slow traffic. We spent 2 hrs in gas station convenient store ( took long time for group to get their coffee and junk food because of other tour busses). Had nice 2hr lunch in small French town. Expected Andora to be quaint but shopping experience was large modern mall.
Overall. Long day. Not much to experience other than looking out bus window at good Mountain Views.

The trip was very nice and the buses were medium size and comfortable. I have be very long legs and I fit 12 hours fine
Also the bus driver was excellent and very smooth. The AC worked very well considering the intense heat wave

We went with Rod and Sergei as the tour guides.

The good:
We had a great time seeing the outskirts of Barcelona. It was a much more relaxed vibe than the busy city. The views were amazing, and Rod did a great job explaining everything.

Of the destinations, we really liked Ax-Les-Thermes. It was a quiet village in France with nice views, weather, and relaxing.

We made stops about every 1,5 hours for a new sight, use bathroom, look at the views, etc. Would recommend to bring some water, as much time is spent driving and also to use bathroom ahead of time.

Improve:

Only things I would say was the air conditioning in the bus. Not much you can do about that then and there. But a little bit of cooler would have added to the comfort.

Overall:

Would recommend for those looking to get a little bit of a taste of each country. It was a nice trip to get away from the city for the day, and very enjoyable to see the country side.

Although the trip was 12 hours long the sights seem on the way was really breathtaking, especially coming from the Caribbean. The stops all complimented each other very well, with reasonable timeframes at each stop. It must be understood that there is a bit of driving of course but the views were worth it as well. Nice compliment to my overall trip to Barcelona

This tour was a complete fiasco. First our guide was late in the morning. We did spend time in Baga which was nice and had breakfast. Second there was snow on the road caused by an avalanche when we were supposed to head to Ax-les=Thermes so we had to go a different route. We didnt spend time at a french restaurant. One of our tour members ended up braking his ankle on a walk across a "private" courtyard by a castle in France so we spent much of our time figuring out where to take him. Eventually we found a hospital which we left him there to be attended to. Due to the wasted time and itinerary completely shot, we spent around 2.5 hours in Andora la Valle walking around looking at shops which you can do at any high end mall in the US. The wife and I did have a good meal at a restaurant in Andorra. Coming back home the view of Monsterrat was beautiful but we eventually ended up coming back exhausted at around 7:30pm. Drained and left unsatisfied. The tour guide tried to make this pleasant for us but not worth the money. We could have used this day to do something else in Barcelona. My advice, if you want to do this, rent a car and explore.

The bus’s policy was that no one was allowed to save seats so it made sitting with family very strenuous. on top of having to rush at every destination because there was barely any time at each stop, we had to ensure to get to the bus 10 minutes early just so my family could sit together. the tour guide was also pretty unhelpful and spent most of the trip talking over the loudspeaker about information that none of us cared about, making it impossible to try to sleep between destinations. I would not recommend this trip.

The views were amazing, even from the bus. We had a few stops along the way for photos. All three places we visited were nice but there was not much time for exploring.

The tour was 12 hours long and, as others stated, it was mostly driving around. We were barely able to go to the toilet and have a bite to eat at each of the locations. This tour should either be longer or something needs to be dropped.
The guide was not actually guiding, he talked a bit in the bus and when we’d get out, everyone would go their separate way.

The driver lacked focused and it wasn’t very safe to be in the bus.

This was truly an amazing experience, led by a wonderful and knowledgeable guide. I highly recommend it. Two pieces of advice for the trip (not criticisms of the tour itself): (1) Bring motion-sickness medication for the drive because the bus was large and it was winding through mountain roads. I get motion sickness on boats, but never automobiles. However, this made me get a little queasy. I was ok after buying some motion-sickness meds in France. (2) This is a very long day (left at 7 am, back in Barcelona around 8 pm). Although you definitely stop to eat and stuff, I’d bring snacks for the bus ride so you don’t get super hungry. Otherwise, do this tour. It’s worth it!

Jordi was an excellent guide. He drove safely and explained things concisely without rambling. He was polite, fun, and knowledgeable. His command of the English language is amazing. He made the tour special. Although it is a long journey, he broke it up into comfortable 90 minutes segments. We enjoyed our stops in Baga, Ax Les Thermes, and Andorra which was our objective. The real treats were not the destinations but more the journey as the scenery is spectacular.

So we did the three country tour yesterday with Explore Catalyuna with Gloria as our guide and Toni as our driver. Firstly, the company was excellent in that the directions for the office and pick up location were clearly marked on the attached documentation. This is fantastic as it alleviates anxiety when trying to find it early in the morning.
So Toni was our driver. Having been on a few tours, I can easily say that he was a safe and 100% competent driver. He also has a sense of humour and interacted with the clients throughout.
Gloria was our guide. Apart from the fact that she new her stuff, she also encouraged the clients to ask questions and shared the responses throughout. She personalised the stops in the Spanish, French and Andorran towns, so that we all got the best of what we wanted, no easy feat. It was her sense of humour and engagement with all of us that we all loved as well. Highly recommend this tour, and if you do book it, ask for Gloria and Toni.

This is the second time we booked a full day tour from Barcelona with Explore Catalunya and it was a great experience to visit Andorra and a few other little sights along the way!
Our guide Xavier was highly entertaining and knowledgeable, ensuring we all had an incredible and memorable experience.
The drive through the Pyrenees is spectacular and on our trip a bit of freak weather for this time of year caused it to snow, which was a treat.
The route passes through many picturesque little villages whilst crossing into France from Catalunya and we had our lunch stop at Ax-Les-Thermes, a beautiful little French village known for its thermal springs.
Whilst the time in Andorra is short and many might only regard it as a skiing destination, it’s definitely a fascinating little country and highly worth the day trip from Barcelona!

Rodrigo the tour guide was a history expert but presented the information in a way that was funny, concise and great for setting context. Highly recommend. And on the way back went around to each person asking if they had questions or needed recommendations about Barcelona.

Drive Franklin did an awesome job on serious mountain roads in rain and fog. Always felt safe.

The tour itself was really cool. Most beautiful unspoiled mountain scenery. Hanibel came through here with is African elephants. The first stop is little mountain town on the Spain side. Cute and lots of history and great architecture. Aix Les Thermes in France was pretty and there are lots of public fountains where you can wade in the thermal baths (it is encouraged). Fabulous lunch and friendly people. Andora was interesting and is known for tax evasion, skiing and shopping so go armed with a list. Great prices on wine and apparently perfume. Turn off your data as it is NOT part of the EU. See the Salvador Dali sculpture in the middle of town.

Wear layers as it is much cooler up in the mountains. 60s in Barcelona and 47 and rain in Andora and some of our group were freezing in shorts and flip flops.

Highly recommend. Great day even in dicey weather.

This was a fantastic side trip while vacationing in Barcelona. Our tour guide, Sergio, was fantastic-so entertaining and informative! While there is a lot of time spent on the bus (that’s how it is when you’re crossing over a major mountain range into 3 countries), the scenery and experience could not be matched. Bagà and Ax-Les-Thermes are beautifully quaint medieval towns. Andorra la Vella is uniquely charming as well. There is so much history in this part of the world, it was a great learning and travel experience!

From the get go, the company was very prompt. We were checked in as soon as we arrived to the office. Our tour guide was Judith .. and just to summit up, she was BRILLIANT! very energetic, attentive and knowledgeable. Throughout the trip she provided a lot of info about the various places we’ve been to. Including, history, urban legends, and funny facts.
Not only this, at the end of the tour, she provided local tips with restaurants, site seeing and entertainment..
one of the best tour guides we’ve been with.
Not to forget, Giovanni, the driver. He was very pleasant, punctual and allowed for a very pleasant bus ride between mountain tops and county sides.

my wife and I really enjoyed this tour. And although it was about a two hour plus ride Gloria made it very informative and fun which made it go by quickly. Also she was very knowledgeable about the places we visited and also gave us her recommendation of places to shop and eat. we highly recommend this tour. Will definitely use explore Catalunya again.

What a great day! Our tour guide, Cam was a delight. He navigated different languages, ages and requests.the time in each place was just right. The stories were told with humor and historic significance. The van was comfortable and observed strict COVID measures. Masking, sanitizers on board. Very reasonably priced.

I’ve had this tour saved for several years as things to do in Spain and boy did it not disappoint. Our tour guide was Rodrigo/Rod and if we could hire to personally take us around Spain the rest of the time we would haha. He was so knowledgeable and came to speak to each party personally about any questions they had to recommendations needed. We had a little over an hour of free time in both Ax-Les-Thermes and Andorra La Vella plus the walking tour of Baga, photo stops of the Pyrenees mountains and a final drink on the way home. You’re never sitting on the bus for more than maybe 2 hours, plenty of bathroom breaks and delicious food. Thank you Explore Catalunya, Rodrigo, Franklin and Julia!

We are happy we went on this tour towards the end of our stay in Barcelona. Since our entire trip was spent in Barcelona it was nice to get out of the city and explore something different. While we gained some fun memories and pictures, the commute is draining. If you hate spending hours on the road in one day, this isn’t for you. Despite the long hours on the road, we don’t regret the experience.

This was an excellent way to see the beautiful scenery of the Catalonian countryside and Andorra. You stop in a few historic and significant towns which now mostly depend on the skiing industry and tourists. You get to go right to the center of Andorra after seeing the beautiful peyronie's. I recommend this tour if you like to see what the countryside looks like, are interested in history or want to knock some towns/cities off of your bucket list.

Our host Arnol was knowledgeable and friendly. I recommend him as your guide.

This was a nice tour, but could make some improvements. Our guide, was EXCELLENT.
The air conditioning on the bus was absolutely freezing in morning and didn't work well at all in the afternoon. They tried to get it going, but it was hot..

The heat isn't their fault - it was an incredibly hot day.

The little village in France was gorgeous. But we spent a lot more time there (2 hours I think?) and much less time in the city in Andorra. I would do the opposite, as there is so much more to do in the city. A lot of people wanted to do some duty-free shopping in Andorra, but we didn't have enough time.

The scenery is lovely and it was a good day.

In a 12-hour (or more) day exploring three countries, three main stops with additional photo stops, it can be exhausting. However this trip, excellently organized by Explore Catalunya, is excellent. Our guide, Sergio, was friendly, knowledgable and highlighted things most would never notice on their own. We had free time to explore but Sergio also started each stop with a group walk and talk about where we were - and this was not only just an intro to the location but a smart and professional way of acclimating visitors to a place before going off on their own to know the surroundings. (Good tour guide strategy as well.) The locations are beautiful, interesting and you do get a definite feel that each stop is a different country. Again, thank you to Sergio who is an amazing guide and driver.

Gloria was a great tour guide who had a lot of energy and thoroughly knew her information on the cities traveled.

The trip was nice and we would recommend it for anyone considering this trip. However, just one suggestion: we would’ve liked less of a guided tour when we arrive to the destination and more free time to wander on our own, because each time, it was a crunch for time. It should be optional but other than that, no complaints :)

It was such an awesome trip!! Our guide was one of the absolute best guides I have had of any tour I've been on. Gloria was very polite, engaging, knowledgeable, personable, enthusiastic, and professional. I could not say enough great things about her. Our driver, Marcelo, was also very good and we felt very safe and well taken care of through out our trip. It was wonderful and I highly recommend this day trip. If I had to give a suggestion or complaint, it would only be to lengthen the trip by an hour to get just one more hour in Andorra. It felt like the time in Andorra was just a little short. The trip really was magical though.

Our family took this tour a week ago and it was a highlight of trip. At first, taking a 12 hour tour seemed daunting, but we had a great guide in Rod and the time seemed to fly. What he said was true that "half of the trip is what you see out of the window." Just spectacular scenery especially going through the Pyrenees. We had a lovely brief stop in Berga (a very quaint Catalonian town), and then lunch and a walk around in Ax-les-Thermes before heading back over scenic mountains (and dramatic switch backs) on the way into Andorra. Totally worth the investment of time. Stunning scenery and a bit off the beaten path. Highly recommend this as do our children. Thanks to Rod and a terrific and skilled driver for making our day!

My older teen son and daughter and I enjoyed visiting Andorra. First we stopped in Baga ES. This is not much more than a restroom break and few minutes walking the tiny village likely due to it’s adjacency to the highway. Then to Ax Les Thermes FR for a bit longer. Then up many switchbacks through a few ski villages over the pass to the capital of Andorra. Here a short visit to the river walk and shopping street. I think our favorite part was the spectacular guide, Judith and driver Angelo. Judith provided just the right amount of history of Andorra and it’s unique relationship to both Spain and France. We had no idea of the unusual reliance and cooperation over time and how skiing has evolved as its industry. Although it was a rare overcast summer day, so the views of the winding roads and peaks were less than typical, the history was fascinating and Judith is one of the better historical guides we have had over the years. Thanks Judith and Angelo.

Excellent trip!! Organised and planned well. Bus was extremely comfortable and the tour guide Judith was very friendly and helpful. She made sure everyone was comfortable and gave some really interesting anecdotes and shared the historical significance of the the places visited. I would highly recommend this

We traveled to France and Andorra and visited many interesting and beautiful places. Our guide Enrique's amusing commentaries added a different angle to everything we saw. On the drive back and forth he also enriched our knowledge of the areas we passed through, about the history and the people.

Our guide Gloria and driver Franklin we're phenomenal. Gloria used humor, historical framing, and respect for the various cultures to make history come alive. The information was paced appropriately and no question was off the table. We talked, walked, shopped, ate, and took plenty of pictures. A must-do trip!

This trip was amazing, we are a family of 5 and wanted a stress free trip we could all enjoy! Our oldest daughter forgot her passport at the hotel and was about to stay behind for the day. However Gloria helped us out by getting her a taxi to get the passport, the bus picked her up on the way out of the city. This went above and beyond for our family, as we could enjoy this trip together. The places we stopped were all very beautiful and interesting. Baga was a quaint small town, we had some delicious croissants as we toured the town. Ax les Thermes was the perfect stop for lunch, a bustling small town with lots of restaurants and shops. We ate our lunch while soaking our feet in the natural thermal waters, it was a beautiful sunny afternoon. Next stop was Andorra, this is a very beautiful country that I learned so much about and hope to return to for a few days. The ski resorts & skiing looked amazing. We enjoyed walking around and visiting many of the stores. After a full day on the bus and seeing so many extraordinary sights we headed back to Barcelona. This trip was better than I had imagined, I loved all the majestic scenery from the bus as well as all the places we visited! Pedro was a fantastic driver and Gloria, was truly the best guide! She was so friendly, knowledgeable and extremely helpful. She gave us so much history of the entire area we covered and was super with recommendations. She took the time to ask all the tour what we would like to do in Andorra and gave us a map to make the most of our time. She gave so many great recommendations in Barcelona as the tour was ending. It was an overall terrific tour and I would highly recommend Gloria and Pedro!

I don’t recommend this tour. So many other ways to spend time in Barcelona, than on a bus for 6 hours. The stop in Andorra was short and the stop in the French town was cute but not worth the price. Tour guide did a fine job. TIP YOUR TOUR GUIDES!
My main complaint is with the passport process into Andorra not in France. Because our passports were never checked in France. And we later found out during our exit from the airport in Sevilla. That we were stamped into Andorra but not out and back into Spain! This caused a hold up by the Guardia Civil passport processor. They questioned us and needed assistance from a supervisor. Shame on this tour operator for putting us in a compromising position!!

Gloria was truly amazing. She was truly invested in this trip and the safety of the crew. She referred to us as “ my beautiful people.” She offered tips for travel, offered to take photos and provided many stories during our travel. This was a full day but truly memorable. Thank you Gloria for a great experience for my mother and I. Highly recommend.

So I really think they need to rewrite the description of this trip . Most of your time is spent on the bus . You get one hour in each town which Iis barely enough time to get lunch . There is no time to soak your feet in the healing waters in France . In Andorra you get one hour and there is only one place that sells souvenirs and there isn’t much choice . Then at the end of the day it’s a 3-4 bus ride home . I would say skip this one if you actually wanting to visit places . If you want beautiful scenery and are ok being on the bus for hours on end then go for it or if you want to buy a cheap electronics in Andorra . The tour guide herself did a great job

This was such a fun tour. It's a long day so be prepared. There is a lot of riding in the bus (which held 20 ppl). Everyone wore masks in the bus so it was totally fine. Our stops were so pretty in Spain, Thermes d'Ax and Andora. The kids (9 and 11 years old) had a great time and were happy to get another stamp in their passports. In France, we ate at the nicest cafe and I probably had the best foie gras I have ever had! My husband had to order a second one. Andora was lovely with lots of shopping. So pictuesque

Being in a bus for nine hours is the down side of it. The rest was very, very nice. The tour guide Miguel was very talkative but you get the feeling that he knows what he talks about. He didn't limit himself to geography. He knew about history, politics, climate, food, and some more. The driver Marcelo is simply a great person. I struck a friendship with his father in law, who was doing the tour with us. Wonderful gentleman.
Bagá is small but still interesting. The bakery has a great croissant. Ax les Thermes is a small town with a great selection of eating options. We had the best croqué monsieur I've ever tried at a pizza parlor suggested by the tour guide. Local cheese and ham that melted in my mouth. I bought some jellies that are delicious.
Andorra has the most breathtaking views, and the weather was nice to us. We couldn't do much shopping since the best watch shops were closed. But anyhow, I would recommend this experience

I most enjoyed the scenery and getting a short visit to the Pyrenees. The French town was interesting, with its history of thermal baths, the market and beautiful river and forest views. The sole stop in Andorra's capital was for shopping. Since I'm not a shopper, that didn't interest me at all.

The guide did his best with a microphone that didn't always work.

The opportunity to visit Spain, France, and Andorra in one day was special. Each stop was unique with plenty of time for self-exploration, shopping, or eating/drinking.
It is a long day with lots of drive time, but the coach was comfortable and the driver excellent. Our tour guide was polite and she mentioned the highlights that we passed along the way.

Rodrigo (Rod) was a were wonderful Tour Guides and driver, and driver Franklin did a wonderful job navigating traffic through the day. Rod definitely knew the history of each region we visited. The historic reference’s immensely helped us to better appreciate how each region was developed over the centuries, to appreciate the cultures, languages, and architecture. Rod was a delight and very informative. He even took the time to gather our passports so we could all get an Andorra passport stamp! Be sure when in Ax-les-Thermes in France to take advantage of the sulfurous hot springs…the water felt so good on the skin.

Overall this was a great trip to see some really interesting places without too much effort. We don't usually do tours but this saved us time on our trip, we didn't have massive expectations but it was a fun day and didn't feel too tiring. All I could say is I with they made time to stop at a few more viewpoints on the way rather than so much time in France, would be a nice extra to just have a few 5 min stops along the way in the mountains.

The best part of this tour was our guide, Gloria. She did such a great job of making sure we were having a nice day and we were all cared for. Our objective for the day was to visit Andorra. Since we have been to Spain and France many times, the additional stops were not as interesting to us, although I am sure they were for many in our group. We loved the stop on the way back to Barcelona that Gloria picked, the views were incredible and we really appreciated that she considered the importance of that for us. It's a long day but, for us, it was worth it to see Andorra with ease.

Great tour! Gloria, our tour guide was energetic, knowledgable, and informative. This is a great way to see more of Europe, in a hybrid guided/self guided environment. After getting the rundown of each region, we were given time to explore alone, which is a great way to explore the area and meet the people. If you're considering this, book it!

Xavier fue nuestra guía. Habla inglés perfectamente porque ha vivido en los Estados Unidos muchas veces. También hay trabajado siendo guía en Africa y otros partes del mundo entonces es muy informado y también divertido. Fija de que podes tomar un café y comprar in croissant o otro pastry en el primer pueblito Bagà. Si tienes que comer sin gluten debes llevar algo por desayunar. Lo pasamos muy buen aprendiendo y riendo.

Xavier is a very professional and experienced guide. He has worked in Africa and the u ores states and has traveled the world working on a cruise ship. He taught us many things and told us the best place to buy chocolate and wine in Andorra. If you go on Tuesday or Saturday there is a local market in the main square of Ax Les Thermes. Immigrants from Venezuela, Syria, China were selling their food as well as a woman selling delicious baguettes and French cheese. Our day was full of learning, meeting new people, seeing new sites and laughing a lot. Xavier was the best. So funny!

It was a pretty long day but this was due to traffic delays because of an accident going out of Barcelona and also coming back. However we had a very informative guide and quite funny too on board. Personally I enjoyed the small towns of Baga in Spain and Ax-les-Thermes. The drive from France to Andorra was pretty spectacular scenery, Shame there was no snow, but blame climate change for that it was pretty warm outside ! I thought that La Vella (Andorra capital) was too touristy and that we did not have much time to walk round, But we lost about an hour due to above accidents etc which did not help.

However, overall it was a pretty good day out.

Kindest regards

Simon

Miguel was an amazing tour guide! He told facts along the ride and made sure we got to see everything along the way. Tony was our amazing bus driver as well. The tour is all day so be prepared to sit, but when you visit these three countries, it is well worth it. Highly recommend the tour if you have the time.

We were a little concerned about the prior reviews and the length of this tour, but we were not disappointed. It is truly a wonderful thing to see the beautiful countryside of all 3 countries. Luda was a wonderful guide as week along with Driver Marcelo who did a great job navigating the winding roads. This is definitely a must do when visiting Barcelona

If you’re short on time, this is a fantastic way to see many great sites in one day. You get to visit three countries without an inordinate amount of walking (brought my 79 year old Dad), and take in a diverse set of vistas across Catalunya and the mountains. The stop at the medieval town gives the trip a beautiful sense of intimacy before the hustle and bustle of Andorra. The guides were truly engaging, well informed and gracious hosts. Highly recommended!

This was by far my favorite part of this trip. Our tour guide Jordy was AMAZING!!!! He was knowledgeable, patient, and a big sweetheart. We loved every part of this. I recommend doing this tour & asking for Jordy. Every place offered a little taste of the culture. The shopping in Andorra was fun and this 12 hour day was worth it. I wish there was more time in each place, but it makes sense for it to be timed the way it was.
I was excited to see "what was next" every stop!

Excellent trip! Professional driver Marcelo, talented tour guide Sergio. The stories were just a perfect combination of history, local specifics and jokes. Staying in the bus was not too tiring and the landscapes would hardly make you sleep. I recommend this highly but make sure you get Sergio as the guide!

Great trip and a lovely way to get to Andorra. Anna was our tour guide and she was amazing. Her knowledge and passion for her job made this tour exceptional. We all learned so much about Spain, France and Andorra. She communicated all day so we all knew what was happening on the tour. It is a long day but so worth it. Highly recommend this tour and if you get Anna you will be delighted.

The entire trip was a waste of time and money. Two small villages we visited in Spain & France were boring and not interesting at all. We arrived at Andora around 2 pm when most stores were closed for lunch, so I could not do any shopping I wanted. In addition, we were given only 1 hour to shop.

The only good thing about that trip was Miguel, the guide, and Marcello, the driver...they both were great.

Worth a visit for these countries in 1 day. Very informative as shared by our tour guide Camilo. He got the knowledge telling us along the way the history of the places we visited. A bit funny with enough sense of humor. I will definitely recommend this tour, if you like history, to all my colleagues who are planning to visit Europe this summer. Worth the money and time.

Myself and my husband Eddie took this wonderful tour today! We LOVED it! Marta (our hostess/tour guide) and Mickey (our driver) were fabulous!! I get quite nervous driving in the mountains but I had complete confidence in the beautiful, comfortable van and the driving ability of Mickey. No fear at all! Marta was a storyteller and full of wonderful information for the entire trip. This is her home, the place and people she loves, places she knows well and has spent time in. She was warm and open to questions and giving suggestions. She made us all comfortable with her humor and warmth! Thank you both! Until we meet again!

Such a great tour! I absolutely loved Ax les Thermes and Andorra. Kam, our tour guide, was great! The best tip that I can offer is to dress warm no matter how the weather in Barcelona. If you’re cold then you probably won’t enjoy the trip as much. Also enjoy the shopping along the way especially in Andorra. Scenic bus ride was everything. Please note the meeting location may differ from the drop off location, both in Barc of course.

Despite the rain it was a very nice day trip from Barcelona. Andorra was lovely and would have liked to have spent more time there, even if it was just the tour bus driving into some of the areas outside of the capital. Our tour guide was very friendly and managed to get our passports stamped with the Andorran stamp! Have already recommended the trip to other friends for when they visit the area

Beautiful scenery driving through the 3 countries, especially through the mountains, but lots of time on a bus driving around. You have lots of stops on the way, but none of them were long enough to do much besides walk around and see the sights.

The cities you stop in are cute! You have time to get snacks, drinks, or quick bite to eat. Enjoyed getting to see new places after being in the major cities this felt more open! Andorra was very different than I was expecting, lots of shopping! We got a quick bite to eat instead.

Our tour guide Robert was nice, we had great conversation throughout the time.

Overall it was a great trip despite all the driving. It was such beautiful scenery, and we learned a lot about Andorra which I never knew!

I felt that tour was good to cover Andorra and a village in France. It might not be exciting as it is lot of travel in the bus but if you want to put a check on covering this beautiful country - Andorra, then it is worth it. I will highly recommend to stay in Andorra and explore Skiing if you can. Though it is not part of this tour. Thanks to Gloria and mick for beautiful ride and guidance.

Gloria, our tour guide, was great! She had so much knowledge, she was super friendly, and also very funny! We enjoyed Baga- but wish we’d had more time in France. Andorra was beautiful to look at, but the stop was mainly for shopping. The only issue we had was that the bus broke down in Andorra. We returned to Barcelona an hour later than expected. Gloria handled this very well and worked extremely hard to remedy the situation. Overall we had a great experience!

Our guide, Gloria, was wonderful.
We visited 3 lovely old towns in the countryside east of Barcelona.
They were 12th century give or take a couple centuries. Gloria gave us a background of the history as well as a walking tour of these delightful places.
We stopped at a cliff.for some photos of the mountain scenery. There was plenty of free time for us to wander.
I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Nice way to see 3 countries in one day. Xavier was good & knowledgeable about the histories/fun facts of the countries. You are in the bus for most of the day, so it’s kinda like a riding tour more so. If you’re not used to sharply curved mountainous roads your should get some motion sickness tables for part of the ride. Overall, I’m very happy I did the tour & got to see beautiful Andorra, a country I would have never thought to visit on my own.

Ana was an amazing tour guide. It was a long day, but she made the tour very enjoyable. The sights were beautiful and we learned so much along the way. The stop in Baga was priceless. From the minute we stepped out of the bus, I felt like we were walking through a story book. It is the perfect fairytale town. Andorra was breathtaking and so was France. I am so happy we went on this tour!!

My wife and I had a wonderful time. Arnold our trip guide was very friendly and very knowledgeable. He explained a lot of the Catalunya history and culture. I strongly recommend this trip to anyone looking for a day voyage away from Barcelona.

The mountains in Andorra are gorgeous and great for pictures. The city of Baga is very cute and charming. Our tour guide was energetic, knowledgeable, kind, and VERY FUNNY! I brought my family (group of 8) and everyone enjoyed the trip. The day is long but worth the time. Highly recommend.

The 2 hours spent in Andorra was absolutely phenomenal! Our guide Gloria and driver Franklin was awesome. She was so well informed and absolutely delightful, keeping us entertained all the way. I would have loved to be able to spend more time in Andorra as this was definitely the highlight of the trip for me.

It was overall a good experience, but there are a couple cons. The first is that with such diverse groups they go different paces, so it was difficult to go at such a slow pace. The other is that I wish we had more time in Andorra; one hour doesn't feel like enough. But as a whole it was still totally worth it

I thought Andorra was an interesting place and was more vibrant than I though it would be. Gloria, our guide, was great and very helpful on whatever things you need in the tour. The downside was that I found Ax Le Thermes and Baga a bit boring, which we could have skipped.

We had a fantastic day! Gloria was such a good guide. She gave the best information and was so entertaining. She even lead a group of us on a little hike to over look one of the towns. Our driver Malcolm was great too. I totally recommend this tour. It’s a long, beautiful day with lots of amazing pictures opportunities, lovely little towns and a comfy ride. We spent 3 days in Barcelona and a whole day out on this tour. Go if you can!

Our tour guide,Arnold, was absolutely amazing!! He made the experience 10x times better. Every step of the way he told us about the history in each place. It was a lot of driving but it was definitely worth seeing all the beautiful parts of Spain, Andorra, and France. It’s a trip my boyfriend and I will never forget!

I was only in Barcelona for a short time so this excursion was a great way to see things I would have done myself if I was staying longer. However in a much more organized and "funner" fashion. Our tour guide Carlos was great. Loved his commentary and energy. Would do this again next time I'm in Barce.

My only regret in this wonderful journey is the time allotted for each individual place, how I wish I could have lingered a bit more. it’s a beautiful destination but made more lasting because of a profound and an intelligent guide named Martha. I love her personal and professional thoughts on everything. By the way don’t forget your anti-vertigo medications because of the winding roads🤪😜

I met and made friends with a couple of like-minded women. Guide was friendly and informative but average based on my life experience. But, really, what made the daytrip for me (and my trip to Barcelona in general) was meeting these two amazing women who were on the tour with me

Locale of start is a little weird— could not find it despite asking at least 5 residents. Bus left without me, on time. No refund. Not really do happy with the whole thing. Better directions might help?

Even though lots of sitting on the bus, is worthwhile to go on this trip. We stop by small medieval village, it’s absolutely beautiful. We had about 45 mins to walk around to explore, move on to the Pyrenees mountain. We rode to the top of mountain, stunning views plus was snowing. Last but not least, the small country Andorra!
If you like skiing, it has lots of skiing resorts, I bet is good place to ski. Overall love this tour, tour guide Enrique was great!

I really liked Baga and the spot in France we went to, both were really awesome to see and walk around at.

Also, our guide, Gloria was very animated and fun to have around throughout the trip. And Pedro was really nice and very prompt at getting us around.

Excellent tour of 3 beautiful towns. An hour in baga lovely quiet old fashioned Town. Followed by small French Town with natural there's and you can put your feet in.
Lastly Andorra beautiful place with some Dali sculptures.
Our tour guide was fantastic and kept us talking all day sergey his name really nice informative guy.

Mini bus was comfortable. There is a few hours driving but as I mention the bus was comfortable enough.

It was a nice getaway from Barcelona and an opportunity to visit diffent places. The guide Carlos and the driver Marcelo were very nice and provided valiable information during the trip. No long or difficult walking was required, so anyone can join this tour. Some great views along the way - which is a plus. I would do it again!

This tour was fantastic! Our guide Sergio was an excellent host. So knowledgeable and friendly. He made everyone feel at home and included. The whole experience was very well done and organized. The locations we visited were perfect.

This is definitely a long tour with a lot of time in a bus, but it was well worth it. The Pyrenees are incredible, and the towns you visit in France and Spain are quite charming with good eateries (and hot springs!). Andorra itself is a very intriguing place. The drive back is also incredible. If there had been bad weather, I think I would have enjoyed this much less, but thankfully the weather was excellent.
Loved every minute. Lots of stunning pictures taken among the Pyrenees. Andorra was beautiful. Duty free shopping !!! The driver Angelo and our tour guide Jordin we’re amazing. Thank you ❤️

The little villas you visit are adorable. The vistas are absolutely stunning. And the food was incredible. But it's a lot of time on the bus. Recommend it however. Will drive it ourselves next time to start as long or short as we like. Request Jordi if you can, he's a great guide and host.

This was an extremely informative experience. Our stop in Baga was short but we got a real feel for the character of the village. The French town of Ax Les Thermes was fun and had a special charm. The food was excellent. Andora was unbelievable.

Anna, and Tony our driver had taken our entry into Andorra from France side to Spanish side. We were very impressed by their professionalism and knowledge.
We look forward to using your tour group in the future.
Thank you

Love this trip. Hopefully you are lucky enough to get Pedro as your driver and Gloria as your guide. Absolutely wonderful. Pedro is a safe driver and Gloria knows all the details and history of the entire area.

Short version: Don't go.

Long version:
This is my first (and hopefully last) 1 star review. It took 49 countries and dozens of tours to actually find something this horrible. I don't even know where to start so I'm just listing stuff here:

-Small group. A minibus full of people = 19 customers / guests. Not so small group. Minibus is otherwise OK as there are 3 seats and a corridor in a row, except for the last row. Last row there are 4 seats but you can't actually fit 4 normal size people there. But yet you do. Imagine sitting in the back with 3 big guys and then try to breath. Now imagine you need to sit there for 11 hours.

-The scenery. Yes, it's great. But you don't see it because you are fighting for your life in the backseat. If you are lucky and are not sitting the be backseat, you still don't see anything as the windows are foggy 98% of the time. Luckily they give you toilet paper in the beginning of the trip (no kidding) so you can wipe the window every 10 seconds if you want to see anything.

-The service. There is none. If you tell the guide that we can't fit in the backseat and it's hard to breath, he answers "Well what can I do". I have a suggestion: Retire as you obviously are not suitable for your job. The proper answer would've been "OK, let's move the _normal size_ guys out from the backseat and try to hand pick the smallest people from the bus to go the the back. Best thing would be not to book 4 people to the backseat at all. It's now 2 days from the trip and my back still hurts because I had to be in crazy positions in the backseat for 11 hours.

-Baga and Ax-les-Thermes. There is absolute nothing to see in these towns. In Baga, there is a coffee and toilet break in which you can burn your mouth with the coffee and still easily be late from the meeting point as 19 people go to the only toilet available. And there's nothing to see which makes the whole stop just a waste of everyone's time. From Ax-les-Thermes you can buy souvenirs from a souvenir shop just like the tour guide says. Except that you can't as the shop is not open at the time you are there. Well, at least you can buy paninis from a great local seller. Except you can't as they have run out of them. Well at least you can go to a free toilet which doesn't have any toilet paper (luckily the guide told this beforehand so just take your own paper with you). The good thing is that you have so little time in both of the towns that you don't have time to get bored.

-The rush. Like said earlier, there's like total of 3-4 hours in the three cities and you probably want to eat something in at least two of them. So you don't actually have any time to do anything else. You do have plenty of time to sit in the minibus though which would be nice if a) you could actually fit in and b) you could actually see out of the windows.

-The choices. Tour guide told everyone to be in the bus exactly 15.30 in Andorra so we could leave before the traffic gets bad. Like you can guess, someone was late for more than 10 minutes and we got stuck in the traffic. The traffic is really bad, it took 2 hours and 20 minutes to get to Spain from Andorra even it's like 10 kilometers. Also remember the cozy backseat of the minibus. Then because of this traffic we also got stuck to an accident site for about 2 more hours. And then we had to switch driver as one driver cannot drive more than 14 hours or so. Which took again more time. We were back in the Barcelona at 23.00 and left 07.00 in the morning. Quite a trip to "sit" in the backseat where's not enough space to sit and breath. The bad choice from the organizer was to wait for the one late hero in Andorra. Better choice: You tell the guests that the minibus leaves at 15.30 sharp so better be there on time. Then it should actually leave 15.30 sharp. Now 18 people had to suffer like 4 extra hours because of one who doesn't know how time works.

I would ask my money back but I read the other "bad" reviews of the company "Explore Catalunya" and no one did actually get a refund in any case. I don't want to waste my time so hopefully you spend my money to either not book 4 people to the backseat next time or to fix the A/C of the minibus so that someone can actually see something from the window.

I'll never again be on your tours. That's a promise.

We had so looked forward to this all day, three country tour. Unfortunately, our guide was not good at all. We were going to be together for many hours, yet he did not get to know any of us.He gave only minimal information, and spent much of the time speaking in Spanish or Catalan to the driver and one woman who spoke Spanish. (This was an English speaking tour)
When we arrived in an town, 15 - 20 minutes of touring, then we were on our own for 45 minutes to an hour plus. We were never given the option of a more extensive time with the guide - he did his own thing.
When we arrived in Andorra, nothing was pointed out except: skiing, and that the country has inexpensive goods.No history, no landmarks, no churches, etc. We had to ask what the people did there, only answer - tourism. I know nothing about this country (sad).
On the trip back we were stopped by Catalan protestors. This was no fault of the tour company or the guide. However, when we finally arrived in Barcelona, two hours late, we were not returned to the travel office. Due to protests we were put on the metro to get back into the center of town. One of the tour group had never been on the metro and did not know how to get to her hotel. the guide said he would get her back. However, the guide got off the metro after only two stops - did not tell us good-bye, or anything. This young lady was devastated (rightly so!!). We ended up getting her to her hotel.
I was very disappointed in this tour - poor guide and did not learn much. I would not recommend this tour unless you make sure you do not have this male guide (I think his name was Esse?? - did not wear a name tag)

My husband had taken ill and was not able to make the trip. I had taken him to the Hospital Del Mar and didn't think to call and cancel. I went on the tour. I was refused a refund for my husband even though there was a woman standing at the counter wanting his ticket. The tour had been full. So the company collected twice on his seat (double dipping) Very disappointed that that is the way you do business. I could understand if the seat had been empty but it wasn't and his illness was an emergency. I want to be contacted about this. gargner @mac.com

My wife and I joined this tour, and I guess our expectations were higher than what the tour turned out to be. Bear in mind we've travelled quite a lot in our lives, so ... maybe we are a bit jaded or more experienced, but ... we always try to be honest and help other travellers with good unbiased opinions.
The medieval towns of Baga, Spain and Ax les Thermals, France were ok. BUT, there's been plenty of European cities, where parts of the city looks somewhat like these medieval towns. It's not that there's that much to see. There were so much shopping for souvenir stores, restaurants, etc., which you can see in most cities, so why pay the high prices and long rides just to see them in a foreign country.
The best part of this tour was the hot thermal springs. I felt we stayed way too long in many of the places, partly because ... I guess we were bored after wandering around and trying to keep busy.
Andorra - we thought the tour here would be more than ... more shopping malls, restaurants, souvenir shops. I guess the highlight was ... statue made by Salvador Deli... whoopee! No castles, no cathedrals. The tour guide, when asked what was best about Andorra, talked about duty free products and joking said "Smuggling is one of the mainstays". To be honest, there's nothing outstanding about Andorra.
AND trying to get a passport with Andorra stamp - forget it. The Andorra passport agents, going in AND coming out, were extremely rude, and refused to stamp the passports, so even the 'highlight' of getting the Andorra stamp on your passport is out the window.
My advice: Big deal about seeing 3 countries in one day. Medieval towns - so what? Andorra? No big deal. Save your money and not waste 12+ hours like we did on a tour that was way too long and way too expensive.
No, we are not bitter. Just being realistic and honest.
Oh, I didn't include any photos in this review, as I normally do. About 99% of the photos taken - if I didn't tell you where it was taken, you might not know where it was!

I loved the trip, we had a great tour guide, She was friendly and had great since of humor. She kept telling stories and some history. It was informative and enjoyable. The only thing that I wished for is to give us more time especially for shopping in Andorra. They were also generous, as they invited us for drinks and coffee at the end of the trip.

The morning started with all of us gathering in the marked address and meeting our guide, Cam(Camilo). There wasn't much room on the bus, but it was still quite comfortable so no issues there.
While driving to Baga, our guide told us about Barcelona's history and a little bit about Baga, it was very interesting. Arrival to Baga was easy, we managed to avoid most of the traffic. We got a little break for coffee there and then a tour in the village with a little story of the history. It was a gorgeous little place. After that, we started driving to Ax Les Thermes, during the ride, guide also told about that place. There, we got around 1.5h of free time to walk around and explore. I advise to bring a small towel for the hot water spring where you can soak your feet. Then when we arrived to Andorra, we got a little stop on the snowy mountain to take pictures - our guide was also very sweet to help us take our pictures. The views were gorgeous. In Andorra we also got free time, either to eat, walk around whatever you want.

In all the places, our guide gave us tips on where to go or what to explore. It was great, we both thought that considering that it was only a 1 day trip, we got enough time in every destination.

On the minibus I sat next to a really nice guy called Bill from the US who seemed to be on the same mission as me: to tick Andorra off the lists of countries we’d visited. And that’s the appeal of this tour - that is what it boils down to. I am a travel dork. This is what I wanted.

But if you’re looking for an excursion or something exciting to do for the day, there are plenty of tours and experiences in and around Barcelona (Montserrat for example) that do not require a 12-hour round trip to a shopping centre in the Pyrenees.

The other countries are almost irrelevant; Bagà (Spain) and Ax-les-Thermes (France) are sleepy and off-season, with very little to see or do except purchase Nutella Croissants.

That said, like Bill, I wanted to visit Andorra La Vella. I’m the type of tourist happy with the novelty value of having gone to Andorra to get a passport stamp, and this is a day trip virtually impossible via any other means (nearest airport is in Toulouse and even the railway doesn’t come close) and so this excursion was perfect.

I would have preferred longer in Andorra but the need for stops given the length of the journey makes that difficult.

The two things that are undeniable:
The professionalism and friendliness of our guide and the driver; and the breathtaking scenery you’ll get to see over the course of the 12.5 journey (particularly at the France/Andorra border).

If you want to visit Andorra: book this trip! If that’s not a priority, maybe think carefully.

We had a very enjoyable 12-hour visit to these countries, and we seem to have avoided many of the issues other reviewers experienced. The stops in Baga, Spain and Ax Les Thermes, France were not exciting but still interesting. Being in Ax on market day was a small bonus, but the main attraction were the hot springs. I would echo another reviewer's suggestion to bring a small towel to dry your feet after dipping them in the pool. Visiting food shops anywhere in France is always fun.
But the best part of the day was the climb up the Pyrenees to Andorra. It snowed a few days before so the mountains were covered with snow and the views were fantastic on a sunny day, The one disappointment is the bus couldn't stop at one of the planned lookout points because it was covered with snow. That meant we couldn't photo the amazing scenery on the climb up. The 2 points we stopped at were still fantastic, but I wish I had photos from before that.
Andorra was fun to walk around. It's pretty much all clothing, perfume and jewellery stores. It was a challenge to find a T-shirt for a souvenir but I managed to. A small bonus is that you'll have an Andorra stamp in your passport (you have to bring it)a and you'll have visited a country relatively few get to.
Lorea was a terrific and informative guide to stores and shops along the way, and also offered a nice premier to the Catalan push for independence.
Judging from other reviews, we apparently were lucky to avoid heavy traffic in certain parts of the trip. It was only quite slow for a short time on the trip into Barcelona. As others have mentioned, there isn't too much leg room between the seats on the bus.
All in all, we really enjoyed this trip and highly recommend it.

Highly recommend this trip with Arnau as your guide. He is extremely friendly, knowledgeable, and very funny - made the long bus rides very entertaining and pleasant.

As for the tour, it is a can’t-miss experience when visiting Spain. Bagá in northern Spain was a beautiful medieval town. We took a wonderful tour through the village’s Main Street and learned about its history - my only wish is there was more time spent there!

Next was a long but absolutely GORGEOUS ride to Ax-Les-Thermes, France. Would definitely recommend exploring the very quaint town first, and then having lunch at the town’s creperie for an authentic French dining experience.

Finally, Andorra! We made several stops here to hike along the countryside and breathe the beautiful fresh mountain air. As a note: we traveled in the middle of July, and Andorra was rather chilly due to the high altitude! Andorra-la-Vella was very high end, luxurious shopping, with souvenir and gift shops mixed in between.

My only disappointment with the trip was the amount of time we had to spend in each place. Bagá was 45 minutes, ALT was about 1hr 15mins, and ALV was about the same. I understand it was a long day - there is no doubt about this! However, I gladly would have paid more money for the the trip if we were able to spend more time enjoying these beautiful places. An hour, give or take, is simply not enough time. Even an extra 2 hours would have probably been sufficient.

This tour is great for people of all ages and physical abilities, with the exception of those who have difficulty with light to moderate climbing. Would recommend to all those to enjoy taking home passport stamps as souvenirs - we left with three new stamps!

The day started normally,, but then our bus broke down 20 minutes into the drive. Then we stood in the street while our guide argued with someone not in our group. Then we walked to a cafe and our guide offered coffee and croissants to everyone while we waited. The wait dragged on and we were there for almost an hour. The initial part of the drive was normal. The rest, however, was not. The microphone on the bus kept cutting out. Then, as the day went on, the bus got hotter and hotter. It was hotter inside the bus than outside. We were all melting and the guide insisted on using the microphone despite it not working and cutting in and out. The drive, which makes up most of the day, was awful. Getting to step out for 5 minutes for pictures in the mountains felt like sweet relief.

When we arrived in France for lunch, most things were closed for break, including the resteraunt we were recommended. The town itself was pretty and had a nice hot spring fountain that we got to soak our feet in. Andorra ended up being just a giant mall, which didn't really interest us.

I wouldn't reccomend this trip.

This was a fantastic trip for my my family (my 7 year old loved it). We were split into two groups, the larger one went to the bus and our group (7 people) got a minivan. The small group made it easy to stick to a schedule. Keep in mind that out of 12 hours you will spend about 8 simply driving. But its worth it - the scenery is fantastic. We had a great guide who gave us plenty of information and lots of time in each city. The only problem was that in a van you don't get the same "wide" view from the small windows. So if you have a choice, pick the bus.

I loved this concept of visiting 3 countries in one day: Spain (Baga), France (Aix-les-Thermes), and Andorra (Andorra la Vella), and a rest stop somewhere in Spain on the way back. Our group consisted of about 17. We rode in a minibus. We started the day by meeting at the Explore Catalunya office (across from Palau de la Musica) at 7am. On the return, we were dropped off at nearby Plaza Catalunya at about 6:30pm. The stops were about 1.5 hours apart. We stayed at each location for about an hour or so. Be prepared for long segments of the bus ride, and the high likelihood of taking naps during the ride.

Baga is a quaint medieval town. During our stop, we were able to get coffee/tea and pastries, and take a quick stroll through the area. The Sant Esteve Church is very attractive.

In Aix-les-Thermes, there are a number of small restaurants for a quick lunch. Also a small outdoor vendor area for food, clothing, etc. Not much in the way of typical souvenir shops (but that's a good thing!). There is a small public pool fed by the hot thermal springs where you can take off your shoes and socks and dip your feet in for a while (bring a small towel). There's no need to have your passport when going from Spain into France; but you'll need it for Andorra (maybe).

At the Andorra border, our guide offered to have our passports stamped. He told us that usually the Andorran officials don't check for passports, but sometimes they do, so you'll need to have them available if you take this tour.

Before proceeding to the capital city of Andorra la Vella, we stopped in the Pyrenees for photo ops. Andorra la Vella is mostly a shopping area.

After leaving Andorra, we stopped at a rest area/cafe somewhere in Spain for a complimentary drink and bathroom break, before heading back to Barcelona.

Overall, a great trip, albeit a long day.

This excursion sounded so inviting. It was a disaster. We left 30 minutes late. We were told we would have croissants and cafe au lait in France - this didn't happen. We went to Andorra - little there outside of duty free shopping. We did enjoy the Dali sculputure, the bridge and the street lights in the ground to help pedestrians who text and walk at the same time. Other than that, not much there - the restaurant we were guided to was not open. Did I mention that we were in the last row of a bus and you couldn't see anything that was highlighted by the tour guide because the windows didn't even reach our seats and our eye level was above the windows? There should be no tickets sold for that back row of seats. That was about an 8 hour torture of the 12 hour excursion. Then on to Ax les Thermes, France - a short stop with no time to enjoy the hot springs, hike, or anything. We had time to eat, walk through a souvenir shop (the only one in the village) and then head back to the bus. Back to Spain and a short stop for a beverage. Then on to a medieval village, Baga, a short walk around - not much to do there as the town was closed up for siesta time. The guide was somewhat informative but he kept the mic so close to his mouth that we were blasted with feedback through much of his presentation. It was very irritating. I would not recommend this tour to anyone. And would not do another tour from this company.

Started on time- with tight schedule to catch a lot through the day. Our tour guide Cam was lovely fellow, very friendly with a quirky sense of humour keeping us enthusiastic with lots of stories & facts!

Quick tips-
1. Be on time & find Tour office on lane right next to Museum of Catalan Music- Staff happy to help. Bus had 19 seats - with just 14 tourists.
2. Baga- Pick up Coffee & Pastry quickly, so u get to complete the short tour with the team. Beautiful alleys to click medieval town pics.
3. Ax Les thermes- Dip your feet in the hot water of natural spring, hike up a bit for a wonderful view of the city (Our tour guide hiked along, sweet chap!), Pick up pizza & stroll around, do visit the quaint little cathedral!
4. Tour bus stopped in 2 locations in Andorra for some scenic landscape with Pyrenees in background-i am gonna frame the pics we clicked, such wonderful views!
5. Andorra- 90min stop sufficient to visit key locations around central street & do some duty free shopping!

Also quick stop on way back to Barcelona where we got free drinks!

Overall it was day well spent & Tour guide Cam made it all the more enjoyable!!

Although I prefer exploring places thoroughly, I also enjoy filling in my travel map. I had originally planned to visit Lisbon, and the only reason I opted for Barcelona instead, is because I realized that I could visit three new countries instead of one. I had no intention of booking this tour, but after looking into visiting France and Andorra on our own, we decided it would be easier to just book this tour, and it didn't disappoint.

Our first stop on the tour was the Spanish town of Baga. This was the least interesting stop on the tour. Based on the pictures I saw, and reading that it's in a national park, I was expecting a tiny stone village nestled on a desolate mountain top. But the "village", which is more of a small town, is pretty well developed, and close to civilization. A mix of old and modern. It didn't really have the traditional medieval charm I was expecting, and looked a bit restored, but the stone buildings and narrow stairways were nice. There's also a nice bakery where you have time to grab some coffee and a fresh pastry before embarking on the rest of your tour. Had I been traveling alone, I probably wouldn't have stopped here, but it was nice to see the contrast between the towns on the French side. Speaking of the French side.....

The next stop on our tour was the charming French town of Ax-les-Thermes. To me this was the most interesting stop on the tour and by far my absolute favorite. It was the only stop where we truly got to take in the local culture. After giving us a tour of the town's thermal pools, Jordi left us over an hour to explore on our own. Some of our group opted to go for local cuisine, some chose to hike to the chapel, and some chose to soak their feet in the thermal pools. We chose to explore the town and interact with the locals. We were fortunate enough to be there on one of the market days, so we got to experience some true French culture. We ended up buying some local sausages and trying a French style kebab, a good option if you want to eat and still have time to explore. The guides have some local friends in town to whom they will direct you, but don't feel obligated to limit your dining options to only these. Despite the reputation French people have, the locals in this town were really friendly and some even spoke fluent English. Do learn at least a few French phrases before coming here. Speaking to them in their language, will make them more willing to speak to you in yours. The drive to Ax was much longer then expected, despite it only being 10 miles from the Spanish border, but you pass through some nice villages and canyons on the way.

From Ax-les-Thermes we continued through the majestic snow covered Pyrenees, on route to tiny Andorra. We were the only ones at the border crossing, so the entire process took maybe only 10 minutes, but about half of that was spent taking pictures at the border. We drove into Andorra, passing by several ski slopes and stopped at a viewpoint overlooking Pas de la Casa. As we began to descent in elevation, the barren snow covered slopes gave way to pine forest, and after about 30 or 40 minutes we arrived at a rural settlement on the outskirts of Soldeu. This was supposed to be the traditional village where we would see what Andorra used to be like. Here we were also supposed to see a Roman church. However, there was nothing really traditional about this village and there was no Roman church. It was basically a restaurant and a few scattered stone houses and walls, which we couldn't even walk up to because they're on private property. And the "short hike to get away from it all" wasn't much of a hike. I was certain the traditional village in question would be Encamp, but they stopped here instead.
