The only Roman, actually they were Romanesque, churches we saw were on the side of the road as we headed towards the capital, and we basically just drove past them. Eventually we arrived at the capital, Andorra la Vella. This stop was what saved the Andorra leg of the tour. Jordi took us to a local restaurant to buy drinks, then gave us the option to either shop or join him on a walking tour of Old Town. I chose the latter. The Old Town was really small, and the only attractions were the Romanesque church, half of which was built from modern materials, and the old building of the general council. There were a few stone buildings but the rest also seemed to be modernized, but it was still more interesting then the ultra modern shopping district. A stop at the Santa Coloma church would have been nice. I feel a little bad here, because Andorra already has a reputation for being boring, and this tour kind of reinforced that notion. There are more interesting places in Andorra they could've shown us.

Our last stop was a restaurant back on the Spanish side, overlooking the ruins of an old castle. Here we got complimentary drinks of our choice, before returning to Barcelona.

Reading some of the reviews, I was afraid I would end up disappointed, but we lucked out and got Jordi as our guide and Alfons as our driver, who was excellent in safely navigating the windy mountain roads. I thought the tour was a bit overpriced at first, but Jordi organized it well, and we got our money's worth.

That being said, the tour did have its cons. The bus seats were tiny and cramped. My mother had to stand up in order for me to buckle my seatbelt. First time in my life I traveled in such a cramped tour bus. If you're a large person, don't even book this tour.
Also, I wish they would pick you up and drop you off at your hotel. The pick up point is in a narrow graffiti covered street, that is basically an alleyway, and on the way back they drop you off at Plaza Catalunya. Since the tour was already costly, we didn't like the idea of having to spend extra money to get to the pick up point, than back to our hotel. Had it been during the day, we would have walked.
Also, it would be cool if they offered day tours to Perpigan. Or that we at least stopped in some of the other villages and ruined castles we passed in France.

All that being said, this tour is perfect if you just want to fill in your travel map. However, there is SO much more to see in this region then what the tour covers, so if you truly want to get to know France and Andorra, you're better off visiting on your own.

Took this tour with my adult daughter while in Barcelona. Almost everyone on the forum recommended NOT taking it but my daughter wanted the passport stamps. The week of the tour the office called to switch our tour date which I agreed to. We arrived the morning of the tour and there were two of the tours going that day. We were put on a van that was NOT for distance travel and it was packed---every seat taken. This vehicle should only be used for in-town tours. It was much too small. The other group was in a larger vehicle with more head room.
Miguel was our guide and there was another guide training that day. It was a rainy day so the the views were not great and we couldn't see much because of the foggy windows. There is no passport stamp when you enter France and we spent only 50 minutes in the small French town. Just enough time for two bus loads to grab a coffee. Thankfully, Miguel did get our passport stamps as we entered Andorra.
Okay, this part is entirely my fault for not doing my research but Andorra is nothing but a giant duty-free mall. If you plan to buy a lot of duty-free items, this might work for you. Of course, make sure you are on a bus that has room for packages.
The highlight of the tour was when we stopped in the Pyrenees for a photo and it began to snow. Honestly, without that stop the tour would have been a bust. If you can plan to go in perfect weather I'm sure the vistas would be great but you are spending a full day in a bus.

My husband and adult daughter went on the trip. Beautiful scenery. Our tour guide was really nice and enjoyable (Arnau)) but our main complaint was the small mini bus. Out tour was full and they crammed us in this small bus with no leg room or any room at all to move or sit comfortable. My husband is 6ft4in tall and my daughter and myself are tall so it was very uncomfortable 12 hours. Not sure why didn't have regular motor coach bus. (the tour we took the day before there was only 11 of us and we had full size coach bus for 1/2 day tour). To much time in French village, only few shops and restaurants open, 30 mins would have been plenty. Not enough time in Andorra. One hour was not enough to shop and eat. Being Christmas time we wanted to do some shopping and it just was not possible to do in such a short time.

Getting up in the dark to meet near the Palau de la Musica at 6:45 am is not vacation fun, but it was worth it to go on this long van ride to the Pyrenees first stopping at Baga, Spain for a restroom break, a white chocolate croissant and great coffee latte, and a short tour of the town, then through the mid Pyrenees and into the Pyrenees to visit the thermal hot springs resort of Aux les Thermes in France at about noon for another bathroom break in a bar where we had a beer and a visit to the hot springs fountain and see California redwoods in a nearby park, then finally we were off to Andorra. Stopped first a the border crossing where we had our passports stamped. No photos allowed there. Then a photo op stop of the Pyrenees that still had inches of snow and then an odd stop for a short hike to see building construction there. Finally we reach Andorra for a lunch break at about 2:20 pm. Andorra has shopping deals for perfume, liquor, cigarettes and gasoline, but Spanish customs limits duty free goods of 2 bottles of liquor and 2 cartons of cigarettes.
Our guide was Xavier who spoke fluent English and quite informative.
We stopped on the way back at a restaurant for a restroom break and a complimentary drink for being good on the trip. We got back at about 7 pm at the drop off point of Placa Catalunya. The tour was limited to 8 people.
Would have preferred if the odd stop were eliminated for more time in Andorra.

We took this tour last week and it was incredible.
With many things being closed on Sunday in Barcelona, this was the perfect day to get out of the city. Essie was our tour guide and he was absolutely wonderful. All three stops were really interesting and I had no idea that we would get so far up into the Pyrenees.
Despite having a completely wretched woman on board with us, he remained very professional and polite, even when she pushed him out of his seat and basically refused to give him his seat back in the front of the bus. This lady was late to the tour and had a taxi bring her all the way to Baga, so she could catch up with the tour. She was late getting back on the bus at one of the stops. Her debit card mysteriously stopped working at one of the stops and he graciously paid for her. Seriously, she was a complete nightmare and should avoid going out in public until she learns common sense, general respect, and decency. Gross! But Essie remained super patient with her couldn't have acted more professional.
We had the misfortune of getting caught in Catalonian protests which caused us to get back almost 2 hours later. Because certain streets in the city were being closed off, Essie and the bus driver made the smart decision to take us to the Metro line, where Essie paid for all of our tickets and rode the Metro with us. He made sure that we all knew where we were going before he departed. Despite all of this, the woman had the audacity to sit down in the Metro and ramble stupid comments about the protests and how she wasn't impressed with our tour guide. We couldn't have been happier to get away from her at the end of the day.
Overall, we were extremely pleased with the tour and feel that our money was very well spent.
Also, Essie was nice enough to gather our passports and make sure that we got our stamps from Andorra. He explained that they don't always have time but that he would try.

Laura from Explore Catalunya was a wonderful guide! She was very knowledgeable and had a very engaging personality. The tour with 13 people was about 12.5 hours long. We spent about 45 minutes in Baga, Spain. We stopped at a local bakery to get their regional specialty and local coffee shop along with a walking tour of the area. It was cold outside so everyone was happy to get back on the van. We spent about 1 hour and 15 minutes in the charming French city of Ax Les Thermes where we had a walking tour and had lunch on our own. I would definitely recommend to dip your feet in the warm thermal baths in the main square area. We walked around the river area which made for great scenery. We stopped at the Andorra border where they stamped our passports. There was a small Andorra sign with their flags nearby which made a nice photo. The Pyrenees Mountains were snow-covered which made for delightful scenery. Another stop was made in an Andorra valley which was also a great photo op also. We stopped in the capital of Andorra, Andorra la Vella, for about an hour and 15 minutes. Besides shopping, I would recommend to walk to the historical area to take a photo of the Andorra la Vella sign on the Pont (bridge) du Paris and the Dali sculptures. All of the time spent in the locations were just perfect. The last stop, to break up the 3.5 hour drive to Barcelona, was in a restaurant near Ponts, Spain where we had a complimentary drink of champagne, wine, beer or soft drink. The only negative was that the van's windows kept fogging up which made it difficult at times to see the scenery and take good photos.

This was a long tour (12 hours) but a very good one. Our guide Jordi was excellent - knowledgeable, entertaining, and considerate. The bus was a smaller one - holding perhaps twenty people total - but it was very comfortable.

There were three stops, the first in Baga, Spain - an old town near the French Border. We stopped at a cafe for food and restrooms. We then had a walking tour around the oldest part of the city. The walkways are steep in some areas - but the walk was not too hard. There were spectacular views of the surrounding mountains and Jordi provided information about the history of this small town.

The next stop was Ax-Les-Thermes - another old city, but in France. It is noted for hot springs that have been in use since the days of the Roman Empire. We had a brief tour of the town - then had an hour to walk around on our own. There were many small restaurants, stores, and shops. We ate at a pizzeria that sold Croquettes and also sampled some cheeses in a local stop. The day we were there, the town was having one of its market days - so their were many vendors selling their wares - from clothes, to fruits and vegetables, meets, crafts.

After leaving Ax-Les-Thermes, we drove through the Pyrenees and over the border into the tiny Principality of Andorra. We stopped right after crossing into Andorra at a lookout from which we could see down into a valley - while the mists of clouds rolled by us from over a ridge of the mountains. We stopped again on the way to Andorra De Ville for more photo ops.

Final stop was Andorra De Ville where we walked around for an hour, looking at sights. The city was a shopping haven - with no taxes on alcohol, tobacco and perfume. So there were many shops - including very upscale establishments. One street was a long pedestrian thoroughfare lined with shops and restaurants.

Part of the beauty of this tour was actually the drive itself - which was largely up in the mountains that straddle the borders of three countries. there were stunning views all along the way.

We booked this excursion from home for one of our days in Barcelona post-cruise last week. We didn't know what to expect...it's a long day, 7a-7p...but it turned out to be one of the highlights of our 12 days in Europe (on a trip filled with wonderful experiences!) Our guide was the AMAZING LAURA...she's professional, knowledgeable, warm and fun. She clearly loves her country and her job and has a knack for making each of her guests (about 20 on this tour) feel welcome and included. The tour visits a small medieval town in Spain (Baga) for a walk and breakfast, a small French thermal spa town, Ax Les Thermes for shopping and lunch and Andorra (with a stop in the beautiful countryside for a passport stamp, a walk and photos and a shopping stop in the Capital City.) The tour concludes with a stop an hour outside Barcelona for a cava and a pastry. The stops are well organized to nicely break up the day...it doesn't feel too long...and we weren't too tired to enjoy a nice dinner out that night back in the city. If you're in Barcelona for more than a few days, I strongly encourage you to book this excursion...it's a memory maker that doesn't disappoint!

Went with another couple - we are in our late 60s. The guide, Arnau was beyond superb - took the time to learn everyone on the tour’s names - 21 total - was quite enthusiastic and knowledgeable - really enjoyable, nice guy. The driver, Jonathan was also very skilled. The bus that seats 27 was quite cramped and uncomfortable - no shoulder room. The best part for us was the first stop, Bagat, a charming little medieval village - Arnau gave us a walking tour before we stopped for a coffee and bathroom break. The drive through the Pyrenees was beautiful - all snowy and big bare peaks. The stop in the little French town was ok: Ax les Termes - but we arrived a little after 11 and that was our designated place to have lunch. Too early. One little restaurant that didn’t appear particularly charming was open and waiting for us but most of our tour mates didn’t go in - kind of expensive menu for maybe good food (will never know) but little charm. The village is small - ski town - with some charming buildings but the shops did not seem to have much in quality goods. The drive into Andorra was spectacular through the massive ski area but the 2 hour stop in the capital town was just awful - ugly, ugly, ugly, modern shopping strip is basically all that is there. Would have much preferred stopping in a medieval village - which there were many along the way on our four hour return (uggh - with one bathroom/drinks stop at non descriptive highway cafe) to Barcelona. Glad I saw the Pyrenees - but might be better to rent a car and do on your own.

We booked this tour based on rave reviews...what a disappointment. The day started off at the tour company’s office where robbers entered the office and stole one of our fellow travelers’ wallet. The tour guide then mentioned that this had happened before and the thieves knew about the company’s routine (so all of us were ripe for the picking!). There was no warning to be on alert INSIDE the office and the staff didn’t even shut the door to hinder the entrance and exit of the robbers. Unbelievable!
Our guide, although a very friendly character, was incoherent in his discussion of historical events and did not have a sufficient command of English to communicate effectively.
All in all, it was a rather horrid experience. The only ameliorating factor was the natural beauty of the land we traversed.

I did the three countries in one day tour with Explore Catalunya. I met for the tour at their office which is only a 5-minute walk from Catalunya square. There were 11 people on the tour the day I went. Enrique was the guide to this day. He was very personable, friendly, and informative. This tour is a long 12-hour day with about 3 hours visiting places and 9 hours driving. The tour consisted of a coffee/pastry stop and a short tour of Baga for about 45 minutes, an hour stop in Ax-les-Thermes around lunchtime, and about a little over an hour in Andorra la Vella. There was also a photo stop and a restroom break. Even though there was a lot of driving, the scenery was beautiful, and I enjoyed just relaxing and looking out the window. It is great for someone who wants to get a quick view and check Andorra off the list. I would travel with Explore Catalunya again.

After booking this excursion months ago, and with great anticipation, imagine our anxiety when the bus’s warning lights came on and a loud grinding of gears ensued. The bus then lurched to a screeching halt. It would not move forward or backward. Our guide consulted the manual. Calls were made. We were descending the Pyrenees at this point. We were just nearing the Capital of Andorra. The bus finally moved but the grinding noise continued. Our driver coasted slowly, even though many of us had great apprehensions and wanted to exit the bus.
When the bus finally stopped, many of us approached the tour guide with our misgivings. Up to this point, he had been disrespectful and rude.
We were told to seek alternative transportation if we did not want to continue riding on this bus. At this point, some of us did just that.
This was our experience in Andorra with this tour.

I was waiting out side with all other people waiting for the tour to start . Stephen come few minutes ago and was explaining to other people be careful from pick pockets. I was having my coffee on other side and then suddenly he pointed out at me he is the pick pocket. Some times they dress nice but in real they are pick pockets. When i said to him that i am also going on tour and i live here. He didnot said any thing and on whole tour he did not give any information when i asked. Persons who want to book tour make sure that stephen is not your guide. Later you will regret on decision. So becareful from guide STEPHEN. Management in office is good friendly and cooperative. No doubt they treat you good. I have my review about guide not about explore catalunya. Explore catalunya is good company but i have expressed my situation how i was treated there by guide. Due to guide i have given negative reviews other wise Explore Catalunys is good. Due to guide behaviour i have to use Trip Advisor normally i dont use.

We booked this tour since it received mostly good reviews, but were very disappointed. In theory the tour could be good, but they did a lot of things wrong that made it not worth the money and the wasted day. First off they changed the itinerary without notifying us. I guess there was an avalanche a few weeks ago in the mountain that made it unable to go to Ax-Les Thermes, but they never notified us of the changes and we ended up in different town. They have updated the tour now, but it would have been nice to know earlier because we were really interested in Ax-Les Thermes and not so much with this new French town. Also the description doesn't mention it but they don't allow food or drink on the bus. You only get a short amount of time at the stops (less than an hour in both France and Spain and under 2 hours in Andorra) and since you can't eat on the bus we had to spend half the time in the towns eating or we would have gone hungry the whole day. There was so much I wanted to see in Andorra but missed out because I was waiting for mediocre food at a restaurant. Also it was fun to see the mountains as you drive, but they only stopped once at a look out above the city in Andorra so don't expect to get many good pictures of landscape scenery unless it's from a moving bus. They also crammed as many people into the mini bus as possible so driving around wasn't very comfortable. Finally the guide was mostly worried about us leaving on time from each place and the small amount she talked it wasn't very interesting. So overall if you like driving around in a crowded bus all day then you will enjoy this tour, otherwise I suggest skipping it.

It was a good trip. We got to see 3 very distinct places in one single day.
Bus that was provided was very comfortable. Our guide was Miguel, who had a very good sense of humor and was very informative.
Best part of the trip in my opinion was the Spanish town of Baga. Seemed like time has stopped here. With the ancient alley ways, bakeries and cafes - it was very refreshing. Next stop was the French town of Aix. Nice thermal springs and charming small French town. Last stop was the capital of Andorra - a shopping paradise - would not be a destination choice I would make personally. But the ride to Andorra was breathtaking with all the snow covered views of the Pyreenes ..
The stops at the various places felt a bit rushed. Would have loved to explore a bit more but totally understandable as we had to cover a lot of distance in the short time we had.
Would definitely recommend.
Sergio was an awesome tour guide! I loved the stop in Ax -les-thermes France was my favorite stop. Be prepared to make some purchases in Andorra! I can believe how inexpensive EVERYTHING was.

This day trip was a great way to get out of Barcelona for the day and see some lovely scenery, quaint villages, and a very unique microcountry. Our guide, Xavi, was super! He went out of his way to make sure we all had a great time on the trip. He even ended the trip by checking with each of us to see if we needed any suggestions for things to do our specific thoughts on the rest of our time in Barcelona. I would highly recommend this tour! It's also fantastic that the tour is limited to 20 people so you don't feel like just another person shoved on a huge bus.

I had a wonderful time during my tour. Our guide was very friendly and incredibly informative. I am sorry to say I do not remember his name, otherwise I would give him a great review specifically. All in all, I would say it was a very good trip for its value. As a solo tourist, I would have liked to spend a little more time in France seeing different towns and country sides, but I understand that time is limited.

Because we wanted to visit Andorra as a country, we joined the 3 Countries in One Day Tour. I found Explore Catalunya on Viator and booked directly with them on their website. The tour required prepayment and it was 129 euros per person. The website was easy to use and payment was easy as well. After I received a confirmation, I emailed them and they re-confirmed.

On the day of the tour, we made our way to their office which is right off Plaza Catalunya (the main plaza in Barcelona). The meeting time was 6:50 am. There was a big group there and they broke us up into 2 groups each with about 15-16 people on 2 separate buses.

Maria was our guide. We enjoyed her and she was able to stress the importance of everyone getting back in time.

The buses were fairly new and had adequate leg room. This proved important because you will spend about 8 hours on the bus. We were given about 1 hour each at Baga, Spain, Aix les Thermes, France and Andorra.

Baga and Aix les Thermes were pretty boring. Maria gave us a quick tour of Baga and Aix les Thermes. During our time at Aix les Thermes, we had a quick lunch. In Andorra there wasn't a tour and mostly just shopping in the area. If you wait to eat lunch in Andorra, there are fast food places. We just walked around for an hour until it was time to get back on the bus.

We left Andorra at around 4:30 and Maria took us to a rest stop/restaurant where everyone was given a free drink (wine, beer, sparkling wine, soda, water, coffee). We left the rest stop at 5:40 and by the time we made it back to Barcelona, it was 7:30 pm.

It is a long day (12+ hours) and I would say know what you are getting into. I read a lot of reviews saying this is a waste of time since the towns were not so great. It would be if you plan to see the highlights of Spain, France or Andorra. That is not this tour. If you've never been to Barcelona, your day would be better spent in and around Barcelona. We knew we just wanted to hit Andorra - it was my 95th country. I had looked at taking public transport just for Andorra and the 3 hour Alsa bus alone would be 60 euros round trip with a fixed departure once or twice a day. So for us, we didn't mind spending a bit more and seeing 2 more not so great towns.

Because we knew exactly what we were getting into, Explore Catalunya provided exactly what we wanted.

This tour takes a very long day out of your vacation, so be prepared. We arrived at the designated tour office early (about 6:45 a.m.), having scouted out the location the day before to be sure we didn’t miss it. As the group gathered, there was suddenly a commotion, as the purse from one of the women in the group was snatched! We understood this was not the first time this has happened. Thieves know the times of group trips, wait along with travelers, who don’t know each other, and then take an opportunity to snatch a purse. While the woman did go on the bus trip, the event delayed us, and added to the anxiety. It also meant that the tour guide was constantly reminding us that we “were already late” so we were rushed in the towns we visited. The first little town (Baga) was charming, with a beautiful medieval square, the coffee shops were clearly expecting us, but after an hour on the small, crowded bus, there was a greater demand for the restrooms than the availability. Again we were admonished to hurry to the bus. The second stop (Ax-les-Thermes) was included for its thermal baths, which looked very uninviting, even if we had had time to use them. Crossing the Pyrenees on the way to Andorra was the highlight of the trip — beautiful scenery! Andorra la Vella, Andorra’s capital, is a modern city with much construction going on. It may be a shopping Mecca and may have points of interest, but we only had an hour to “have lunch and walk around.” We went to a restaurant recommended by the guide, bolted our great lunch down, dashed back to the bus, only to be admonished again because we were five minutes late. We got back to Barcelona in time to be late for our dinner reservations. Plan for an entire day, sitting for most of it on a small bus. If we were to explore this area again, we would hire a private guide and design our own route.

Our guide Sergio was hilariously entertaining and informative and our driver, Bilo, deserved kudos to the moon and back for navigating those crazy mountain roads.
Our group of 4: three adults and one teen decided to give this day trip a try. When/where else can you visit 3 countries in one day? What an extraordinary experience we had taking this day trip on Oct 12/17. Albeit an early morning, the group of 23 was all on time and we loaded into this very well kept, comfortable mini bus and were off to our first stop in Baga, Spain. A beautiful tiny town, just waking up, located in the pre-Pyrenees foothills. The drive from there into France (Ax-les-Thermes) was stunning and there were several moments when my breath was literally taken; it was so beautiful. The quaint french town was everything and more that you would expect and we enjoyed some delicious crepes at the outdoor cafe of beautiful L'Oiseau Bleu. There were several stops throughout the trip to see the incredible mountains and take in the sights. The stop in Andorra was very commercial and for those that like to shop, was a lot of fun. We made a stop in the Incles Valley which is a typical old town of Andorra, and is stunning though the altitude can make for some shallow breathing. This is a long bus trip and is broken up very well. Our guide made it extremely entertaining and fun. Definitely worth the time and money.

We did this tour on Saturday 6 July with professional guide Mateus and driver Marcello.

Whilst it was a long day, it was professionally organised and our time was managed well, with sufficient free time to take pics and explore.

Mateus was a great guide, providing extensive information and sharing his knowledge in clear and concise English.

We loved this day trip!

I don't know where to start. This was definitely a day well spent. Our tour guide, Alexandra was exciting, inspiring, and very knowledgeable. Even though our day started early, our first stop in Spain included pastries, and coffee. We visited the quaint town of Baja, where we were able to pass through on Market day. The merchant even let us sample some of his wares.
The next stop we were able to dip our feet into the Therma Spa waters in Ax Les Thermes. It was a little too hot, but I couldn't pass up the chance to dip.
Our last stop was the beautiful, unique country of Andorra. If you are looking for a different lace to Ski, then this is the place. I highly recommend it.

Our tour guide was Gloria and our driver was Tony. Each town in Spain, France and Andorra itself was so beautiful. I feel that the trip is value for money and the sights were stunning. Gloria was fun and her English was pretty good. The day is very long and quite draining but is really worth it in my opinion. I highly recommend it.

Having started the morning with a group member suffering a snatch & run robbery outside the booking office at 7.05am, we thought the day would be a downer. Our guide (Gloria) saw the incident & chased the miscreant but without avail.
So with that as a prelude, we jumped on the bus & headed for Baga. A quaint small brown town with some lovely Spanish history. A quick few snaps & then onto France. All the way, Gloria was informative & engaging & employed her own 50/50 rule for quiet times/discussion. Kudos for that as a few on our trip were jetlagged.

Hitting France we had a great treat with Gloria's countdown for the border crossing & a well rehearsed impromptu chorus of "The Marseillaise".

On stopping, we loved interacting with the locals in our cross Australian/French accents (we call it frogwaāre).

The local spas at Ax-Les-Thermes were nice for a toe dipping.

A quick bite & on to Andorra, again, Gloria was full of facts & trivia & regaled us again with her wit the whole time.

Andorra is no doubt a winter haven but we enjoyed it's simple unique charm on a warm day. It's a movie set of ski fields, cows with bells & low tax shopping.

Back on the bus & vamoose back to Espana.

If I was rating Gloria I'd say ☆☆☆☆☆ but the trip is a long day & there's many kms between attractions. It's a bucket list ticker from the fact you see 3 countries in one day, but if you had a poor tour guide, you may not have such a great experience. So to recap, Gloria was glorious.

We had a great experience with Sergio and the tour over all. It was amazing to see the Spanish, French and Andorran country sides with some very nice stops all day long. Not only were we immersed visually, but Sergio had described the history of the areas as well. I would highly recommend this for anyone. It has a good amount of walk and rest and plenty of chances to rest as well, if needed.

Xavier our guide made the tour worthwhile. He was jovial, knowledgeable and gave a history of each of the location. We went to Ax, France which is a small quaint village, they had a small food market
The next stop was Andorra. We even saw snow, Pyrenees Mountains are spectacular. Back to Spain, the mountains are breathtaking. We can't forget our driver Alonz for getting us to our destinations.

First the tour is for the nature lovers not for the selfi freaks. Yap most of the time of the tour u will be in the bus but the outside view is worth watching. Our super guide ESSICEand driver TOMY gave us a awasome time from Barcelona to Andorra through France. The first stop is the sleepy town of Baga. Basically it's a breakfast stop in a calm country side. Then all the way to France. Hot water fountain is a nice break in the journey. Last Andorra..... The beautiful snow covered city.

We really appreciated this tour! My husband and I had a limited time in Barcelona and this helped us to feel like we were able to see so many sites within the time we did have. My favorite part with Southern France when we were able to put our feet in the hot springs. I'm not sure why that was so cool, but it was. I brought a towel and easily cleaned up when I was done. The views of the mountains were breath taking.

Oir guide, Miguel from Explore Catalunya was awesome! Danny our driver was fabulous! We took a minivan that seats 25 pax from Barcelona to Baga, Spain..it was -1C...cold but quaint town was worth a visit. We were lucky that the priest in the town church arrived while our tour guide was explaining about the church and we were alllowed to enter the church. Inside was a replica of how the town looked loke centures ago, and we were shown an 11th century cross! Next stop was Ax les Thermes, France, where we were able to dip our fit in very very very hot sulfur-smelling water, but it allowed our feet to relax and it was a great experience. On we go to Andorra, traffic was bad in the Pyrennes, yes, can't believe it, so we run short of time and had only an hour to see the capital. Made some shopping and took some photos. 2 hours would have been awesome. The drive back was foggy and cold but the minivan temp was comfy. We stopped for a drink on our way back to BCN. The tour was long and tiring...12hours..but it was well worth it. One could probably get to these places on their own, but it would have been difficult. The history as well as jokes made by Miguel made the trip all the more fun and exciting. Two thumbs up to Miguel and the tour!

Although this is a long journey for one day, visiting Andorra and the Spanish and French towns in the Pyrenees is a must if you have extra time in Barcelona. Our guide was wonderful and explained numerous facts about the area and especially Andorra. Cost was reasonable and the bus was comfortable. Consider this trip!!!

Booked this trip and wasn't disappointed!
Was a long trip with alot of traveling but the views from the bus were stunning!
Our guide was very professional and friendly I think he said his name was arnauld or somthing similar ( apologies if this is incorrect ).
The downsides are you don't get too long in each country, maybe a hour to hour and a half. But don't let this put you off as the views from the coach were as amazing as stopping in Spain France and Andorra.
The guides also made regular rest stops on route during the day including a drink in a bar on route back to Barcelona.
All in all, had a brilliant day and would recomend !

It was a full bus but our guide ,Xavier was good,compassionate and so knowledgeable that we feel so relax even with strangers in a minibus.awesome view,ate croissant and crepes in Ax les Thermes.we were fortunate enough to be in Ax les Thermes on market day,i bought some tableclothes ,torrones and cheeses at cheap prize..Andorra was a surprise ,to see this very enterprising place with all the highend shops on top of the mountains.it was an amazing tour.i highly recommend to my friends and family.
Did this trip 5th August 18 by myself it was a awesome trip well worth the long day.Our guide was great could not fault anything.I would do again.

Fellow travellers have already reviewed this trip well. Thank you for all the tips from being vigilant against would-be thieves at the start of the tour to bringing something lightweight but warm in case the weather is not so warm in the morning (even in mid August). Miguel our guide and Rafa our driver were exceptional. Making the tour and long drives go smoothly. We were told some of the history of Baga (Spain) and Ax- Les-Thermes (France). Yes, the Andorra was much a shopping trip (unless you absolutely did not want to shop), we didn’t find prices any cheaper than a typical international airport duty free section but it was a nice touch to get the passport stamp😀. Trip positives were the beautiful sunshine all day, the stunning scenery, seeing quaint villages and great pastries in the village cafes. Our highlight was being able to dip our feet in the hot thermal spring in ALT. So much so, we didn’t see so much of the village. As other travellers have said, having a bit more time there could have allowed us to really see the villages! This for us was the only downside. Other than that a great way to say you’ve visited three countries in one day😀. Also a suggestion: the really scenic route appears to be on the outgoing leg of the tour, so seat changes to allow all passengers access to the views should be made earlier.

Thank you Miguel and the coach driver for a wonderful tour. Commentary, scenery and facilities were all on point. However, it needs to be mentioned that sitting in the back row of the coach does not allow for ideal viewing of the scenery. You need to look at moving pax seating arrangements during the tour so all individuals equally get to truly enjoy the stunning landscape. 🙏
I did this trip with my daughter. Although a lot of time was spent on a tour bus, is was small and very comfortable. Never knew Andorra existed!! Breathtaking views.

Being a mobility challenged person with prostheses, I was a bit worried that I may not be able to do the pace and slow everyone down. Sergio our guide was superb ! I didn’t stress out at all and is the highlight of our 3 weeks cruise/tour in Spain and Portugal. This tour is even better than those organised by our Oceania cruise ship. Totally recommended for mobility challenged people. Make sure you let the guide know in advance to let you start walking first.

Sergio, you are the best !!!

There are several companies that offer this tour. We did this primarily as it’s really the only way for a tourist to see Andorra.
There’s a lot of time on the bus but the scenery was gorgeous.
We had a snack at Bagas, Spain and had some free time to wander about the medieval area. We had a short but good small walking tour.
Then onto a longer stop at Aix les Thermes where we had an excellent lunch, enjoyed the super clean free thermal waters in the middle of town, picked up some local fruits and baked goods at the small farmers market. Very pretty town. Then on up and through the Pyrenees to Andorra. The mountains were still snowy in late May. The stop in Andorra la Vella was a disappointment. Shops were not special. Would rather have spent more time in the countryside where we did have a quick look at stone huts and gorgeous mountain meadows.
On the long trip back we had a quick stop for a complimentary drink.
A tourist would never be able to do this much on their own.

I actually enjoyed the time on the bus, just watching the gorgeous scenery. Of course, we had lovely weather so that helped--I wouldn't want to try the road through Andorra in the winter!. Unlike other reviews, I didn't feel rushed at all. We decided to have lunch at Aix-les-Thermes instead of Andorra (shout out to Couteaux Fourchettes who served us a delicious fixed price lunch at the ungodly early hour of 11:30 a.m. knowing that we had to be back on the bus by 12:30). That gave us time to poke through the clothing stores in Andorra and left plenty of time to have a glass of wine before relaxing on the bus again for the long ride back to Barcelona. I thought it was a great (although long) day and a nice way to get out of the city if you have an extra day. (Do remember you MUST bring your passport!)

An early start to the day helped by the noisy night spent in my accommodation keeping me awake. I slept part of the way to the first stop at Baga. This is a splendid little village with some wonderful architecture and immense views. The village had a really sleepy peaceful feel to it and was somewhere I’d have happily spent longer in. But alas we had to push on to Ax Les Thermes, crossing the Fench border. But unfortunately our journey into France ended when an avalanche blocked the roads. The guide did his best to remedy the situation and treated the group to a drink and a snack at a French cafe before returning to Spain. On returning to Spain an impromptu stop in the town of Puigcerdà and a pretty lakeside walk added an unplanned element to the day. Then back to the bus and onwards to Andorra. Slightly disappointed with Andorra as I had probably expected something of a tour before free time but it proved to be just free time for shopping. Which wasn’t really what I had in mind. But happy to have ticked of another country at least. The trip back to Barcelona was broken with a stop at a road side diner. Where the guide bought us all a drink, I wouldn’t recommend the house red wine at this stop. But the guide and the driver where excellent and obviously disappointed to have missed Ax Les Thermes but couldn’t ask for better staff.

Hilarious tour guide and an excellent driver. The names escape me but someone was named Isidro and the driver was from Ecuador. Mainly took the tour just to cross Andorra off the list of countries visited but enjoyed it very much. I assumed the France part was just passing through on our way to/from Andorra but that was wrong - France was a stop in itself. The tour stops every 1.5 hours for breaks so the first is in the very old city of Baga. Because of the recent snow, we couldn't go to their usual stop in France so instead went to the citadelle city of Mont-Louis. The snow falling in the pines was just so beautiful. As it was the holidays (and due to the weather), traffic slowed us up a bit, leaving only 1.5 hours in Andorra. Andorra is beautiful, set in incredible mountain valleys, but it's quite the traffic jam from shoppers and skiers. Spent the 1.5 hours having lunch and then looking all over for a souvenir stand. The stop on the way back includes a free drink. The tour took a little over 12 hours. It's not in a huge bus, there were 19 of us.

We did the 3 countries in one day tour with Arnold as out tour guide. It was a beast of a day but so very wonderful. Arnold was entertaining and knowledgeable. He made sure everyone had a great time and had recommendations for us for other sites and dining in Barcelona. Would definitely take another trip with him. Andorra was amazing. This is a great trip.

I really enjoyed the day that my mom and I spent on this tour. The tour guide was very informative and he was patiently waiting for my mom to be able to catch up with the group. We made a stop in Baga, to have a quick coffee time, in D'Ax Les Thermes for a hot spring & possible chance for early lunch and Andorra for lunch. Unfortunately, I don't think they gave us enough time for a true shopping time in Andorra since it was 1 hour and 30 minutes for sightseeing in Andorra la Vella, lunch, shopping.

I really appreciate the fact that he stopped by the border and got us a stamp on our passport for Andorra.

We took this trip as part of a long weekend in Barcelona. You leave with around 10 other people in a comfortable minibus from the opera house in the city centre early in the morning - around 0800, and drive up into the Pyrenees, crossing into France and stopping for food and drinks at a lovely spa town before heading higher and into Andorra, where you can get a celebratory stamp in your passport. There is a stop in the main town of Andorra which is given over entirely to duty-free shops - rather like the Las Vegas strip dumped into the middle of the Cairngorms national park! The drive back through Catalonia is lovely. You get back to Barcelona around 2000. A highly recommended tour
George was a fantastic tour guide. Informative, well spoken and a good guy. Beautiful countryside. Andorra was a special place to visit. Low prices too!

This was a glorified shopping trip with over half (7 hours!) spent in a speeding bus. 1st and second stops were good then at the main stop, they drop you off and say”shop, you have an hour” Nothing at all special about the shops. All big retail. Also they are not sensitive to personal needs. Very little access to bathrooms including one 2 hour stretch on the bus just after lunch. If you have any physical issues, do not take this particular trip! Scenery is beautiful. More photo stop would have been nice. Just not worth the money.

We had so been looking forward to this tour--and it could have been pure delight, except we wound up losing the lottery.

On the day of our tour, they had robust bookings and so used 2 travel vans. The one was newer, had generous windows, was bigger and presumably had bigger seats. The one my wife and I got onto was older, smaller and inferior. The seats were on two levels. If you were in the front 3 rows (as we were half of the time) you got to see the views out the windows--if you were on the three rows of elevatred seats you still had some views--but the rear bench seat, allegedly holding four but unless they were children they didn't fit AT ALL--were like travelling in a box, rarely seeing out the window to enjoy the sights.

Seating meant that, when stopping in little towns, you either got back to the van early to line up for a prime seat--or you got stuck in the box in back. Frankly, I'm offended that they should collect full price from us all and not give us all an equivalent experience. The company should get rid of he old bus or at least remove that back bench seat, which actually caused me pain as I was crammed into it with three other full sized American adults.

Moreover, our tour guide, Nicholas--what a great fellow, affable and full of knowledge about history, art, politics, even geology. I had no issues understanding him when we were off the bus touring towns, but on the bus, half of what he said was incomprehansible due to the sound system. The directional microphone he held dropped volume unless he kept it firmly in front of his mouth--a challenge in a moving bus for hours. Moreover he had no monitor and ofren the system would shut down and people in back would shout "can't hear you!" and he'd correcr. Finally the old sound system was just a bit tinny and crackly--not as bad as many transit systems, but just enough to blur his diction.

The tour itself is well conceived. The one-hour stop at each location seems a little short for Andorra la Vella but just fine for the others Take along a towle for Ax-les-Thermes, there's a public pool where you may soak your feet, so get a take-away sandwich for lunch and plan to be luxurious.

In fhe end, I think I deserve a refund. At any given time, the other busload was probably getting an excellent tour, and the eight people in our front three rows also--but half of he trip I was uncomfortable, cramped, and missing the tour guidance that I craved to hear. If you're gfoing to have inferior seating, then assign seats when booking and give people the option of a discount for the poor ones--and a steeper one for the horrid ones.

This is a must for everyone who has not done this trip through the stunning high snowcovered mountains in Andorra. The local train from L´hospitalet on the french side to Toulouse and from there to Lourdes, the city of miracles.

The tour was exactly as billed. The guide was friendly and very knowledgeable. We stopped in towns in Spain, France, and Andorra.in each town we had time to get a bite to eat, to shop, or walk around. The bus was comfortable. Two important things to note. First, bring your passport as the brochure stresses or you cannot go—2 people learned that the hard way. Second, no restroom on the bus. Overall, I really enjoyed it.

Recommended. This was a great day.... however long. But you are visiting 3 countries in one day. The driver was great , our guide Lorea was extremely intelligent and gave us lots of wonderful information about the area and the culture. She was the best part of our day.
It was nice to get out of the typical Barcelona tourist attractions and get to see the country.
It’s a good idea to plan the trip the day after you arrive bc you get some good nap time on the road.

We took this tour while visiting Barcelona last week. The tour operator was extremely knowledgeable and provided us detailed information about all areas during the trip. He was fantastic.

The towns we visited were spectacular and we were able to spend time walking around and even eating at various local places.

I really enjoyed this trip. It was a beautiful ride (small bus) through the Spain and France countryside, and then into. Andorra. Xavier was a great guide. Honestly I didn't need the duty free shopping piece in Andorra but I understand why people would like it. It was only an hour of the full day. The rest of the trip is well paced with several countryside stops for both pitstop and scenery. Ax Les Themes was a picturesque town as you would expect in France. Each shop specializing in one thing.. cheese, bread, coffee, pastry. Lovely.

We loved this tour. Our guide was wonderful and patient. The bus was very comfortable. We had just enough time in each place we visited. Andorra was our favorite. Each stop is timed nicely so you aren’t stuck on the bus for extremely long periods of time.

I’ve been on better tours, I’ve been on worse tours. There’s a lot of bus time involved in this trip, and despite what other reviewers have said, there really isn’t much time at each of the stops. Overall I felt that the description of the trip over-promised and under-delivered.

The drive itself is quite lovely— the scenery IS gorgeous—but the stops themselves are disappointing and the descriptions were somewhat misleading. Yes, you see a lot of stuff, but much of it is from the bus as you speed by.

We left Barcelona on time at 7am. The first stop was the small town of Bagá, where we were given just a few minutes to buy croissants at a bakery. There was no time to buy coffee or eat— we had to eat while we walked. After our brief tour of the town, we were given 5 minutes to use the restroom in a local bar before we were expected to be on the bus.

There was no breakfast in France, no croissants and cafe-au-lait in Mont-Louis. From Bagá we drove to Ax-les-Thermes, France where we again had a brief tour of the town and then were given just under an hour to eat some food and explore the town on our own. Restaurant options were limited, particularly considering the few restaurants available would have likely required the full hour to get served and pay (it’s France, after all!). The women noted that the restrooms offered to us required a squat (no proper toilet) and that at least one of the stalls lacked toilet paper.

From Ax-Les-Thermes we traveled to Andorra where we had our final small tour and a chance to do some duty-free shopping. The time we had there was adequate, but the educational aspect was lacking. The description makes it sound like you have flexibility to eat and then hike or explore. You have time to either shop or eat. And there was no mention or suggestion of a traditional Andorran restaurant.

For the price and based on the description, our group expected more. For $150 USD approx person, you could easily rent a car and have money left over for breakfast, lunch, and shopping.

First of all, without tour guide Arnou, and driver Jonathan, this tour would not have been as pleasant as it was! They were excellent in their respective jobs. Arnou's knowledge of the sites passed through and visited was also most informative, and the planned stops were scheduled to accommodate people's human needs breaks. However, the tour could have been improved by spending a helluva lot LESS time in Andorra's capitol (who needs to go shopping for two and a half hours on a cultural tour?), a lot MORE time in some of the quaint medieval towns we passed, and replacing the last pitstop also with a more authentic Catalunyan experience than the 'side-of-the-road' place we did go to! Otherwise, the trip was a success! Great photos of some unique places!

Our Tour started at 7 Am form Barcelona and was about 9 hours long First wee went to France Mount Lowe nice beautiful small town with hot water springs and small friendly bakeries with delicious pastries and hot chocolate . them we move the picturesque Country of Andorra la Bella. Did not know it existed very nice and very pretty in the middle of the Pyrenees. It was a great trip with a great turists guide Matias. Definitely a most if you are in Barcelona.

We had looked forward to this trip but felt that it was a lot of time spent driving in the bus. The 3 stops were interesting and the time spent at each site was sufficient. However, it was definitely not worth the 11 hours that were spent visiting these places. And we were not that thrilled with any of the places we visited. This was not a tour I would highly recommend.

Went on tour and was a great experience. Loaded up early AM at the office, it was still dark outside, but this is a 12+ hour day so be expecting this. Went right away to the bus which was approx 24 people - every seat was filled up. This is mainly a 3 part tour. First part was a visit to small local town, not much but it's a stop to eat breakfast.
Next was a cut French town that is known for its hot springs. Nice to dip feet into the hot spring pool but not much else to see, it's a nice town and time to grab a quick lunch on your own, but note you do not have a lot of time. I found lunch & ate fast.

Next was visit to Andorra. This was great, the only snag on our trip was that the border control on the French side was backed up so we waited in a huge line of cars and burned 90 minutes just sitting there before we had our passports stamped. Since this wasted much time, we only had 1:15 to explore Andorra. This is not nearly enough time to do some serious duty free shopping of the high end goods that Andorra has to offer. If you are thinking of going to visit Andorra and expect to do some major shopping damage, you will not be happy on this tour. You will need at least six hours of time and this is not the tour for you. Lucky me I did not intend to do much shopping and did not, there wasn't any time for that, so sightseeing was enough for me. Andorra is a beautiful place and the tour guide provided a very nice knowledgeable description of the sites and some history, but no shopping time for sure.

Overall was a good tour, but make sure you bring water, a jacket since the morning is very cold, as it gradually warmed up by the end of the day this time of year. If you go when it's cold you might not get up the roads to Andorra using the route we took.

Spent a huge amount of time in the bus, about 8 or more of the 14 hours we were in the tour, so don't say I didn't warn you. It's a lot of bus driving and sitting time.

If you are intending to shop in Andorra, you should go there on your own, maybe spend one night over, and do it right, not rushed on a tour like this one.

What a way to spend a day out of Barcelona. This tour provides a great opportunity to experience the countryside of both Spain and France as it transitions from rolling hills of vineyards to the majestic Pyranees. We stopped in the quaint medieval town of Baga Spain with its sandstone buildings, followed by Mont-Louis France, a more modern French town with more orderly streets and stone, brick and stucco structures in a variety of colours. Andorra sits high up in the Pyranees, has 80,000 inhabitants, and clearly substantial wealth. The main town here, Andorra la Villa, is really a resort town with a focus on tourism and in the winter, skiing. There is even a McDonald's, featuring a "McAuto".

It was a great tour and our guide (Laura) was excellent and very obliging. Our driver was awesome and patient, which is very important on long trips like this--but his driving was impeccable and he remained very polite. We had heavy traffic on the way back from France into Spain, and what should have taken 2 hours took about 4 hours. Nevertheless, the day went well. We went first to Baga, a medieval Spanish village, then Andorra (we went there before France because of the anticipated traffic from France), and then Ax les Thermes.

Seeing 3 countries in one day (although tiny parts only for Spain and France). Guiseppe (driver) and Felicidad (guide) are super! I particularly like Baga and Aux de Theme. The bus is v convenient. The stops in between is just arranged super nicely. Highly recommended

This was a unique adventure. Being able to see different cultures and view the villages in Spain and France was wonderful. Andorra was a new and great experience for us. Our guide, Xavier, was personable, knowledgeable and experienced. We highly recommend this trip!

We had to meet our guide, Anna, at 6:45 AM. Our first stop was the small medieval village of Baga, Spain. Anna led us on a short walking tour there giving us a brief history of Baga. We then had some free time to explore on our own. We then headed to Ax Les Thermes, France. Anna gave us an overview of the city and led us to the thermal pools. We had time to soak our feet there. The water was quite hot! We later met up with Anna again and she gave us some recommendations for lunch. We then made our way through the Pyrenees Alps to Andorra de la Vella. Here we had time to take advantage of their duty free shopping. It was a long day but very enjoyable. Anna was a great guide.

After reading some of the reviews, I thought it would be difficult to spend so much time on a bus. However, we had a great tour guide, Sergio. Also, we stopped every 1.5 hours or so. I slept most of the ride anyway after a long walking day before in Barcelona. I liked getting out of the city to explore areas I wouldn't have. I loved all three spots and the few extra stops (a natural waterfall and old area of Andorra). Going to Andorra was pretty cool since I know I'd likely never visit that country. Nice to have a passport stamp too. The worst part was driving up the mountain from France to Andorra. IT'S SUPER CURVY. If you get motion sickness, don't do this trip. Otherwise, bring a book and/or headphones for the ride.

My husband and I booked this tour and had such a great time. There is a lot of drive time, but the places you see are totally worth it. The little villages and huge Pyrenees are absolutely beautiful. Laura was an amazing tour guide. She is so personable and funny. On our way back to Barcelona, we stopped for Cava and a delicious pastry ( I’d love to know the name of it.... it was delicious).
We highly recommend this tour!!

Maria was our guide and she took our group of about 20 people to Bagà, Ax-les-therms and finally Andorra. Except for Andorra la Vella which is basically a shopping district, the rest (especially a short walk in the countryside in Andorra) were lovely. Maria kept us informed with loads of interesting facts and stories but gave us enough time to ourselves too.
The minibus was comfortable and we were back in town by 7:30pm after leaving at 7am.

Thank you to Steve for being a lively, informative and patient tour guide! We had a wonderful time today exploring Bagá, a charming medieval town that happened to have an excellent coffee bar with a farmers market pastry stand just out front, then on to Ax-les-Thermes, which was nice but too rainy and slushy to enjoy properly, followed by lovely Andorra, with its excellent shopping and Dalí monument. Along the way, the white-snow-covered Pyrenees were breathtaking.
Thank you for a very memorable day, Steve! We also appreciated your recommendation for a tapas place close by. I just wrote a 5-star TA review for El Nacional and gave a shoutout to you for the recommendation.

This was a long, but really great day. We went in December so Andorra and the mountains were especially beautiful. Ax Les Thermes was just sort of ehhhh. Baga was very small but beautiful and interesting. Be prepared to shop in Andorra as the only realy stop is the shopping area and its BUSY. . We did stop to take photos of the views etc and honestly, the most amazing views were at passport control in Andorra. Overall a super cool tour. Very windy roads so if you get motion sick in the car, be prepared.

What a wonderful way to easily get to France and Andorra and have everything taken care of for you! Loved getting to a quaint French village enjoying the market and getting an incredible lunch at a little cafe.

Then getting to see the breathtaking Pyrenees Mountains and Andorra. The day could not have been more enjoyable, loved getting to see 3 unique places in one day!

Do not hesitate booking this tour if you want to experience 3 countries in one day!

We had an amazing time !
Gloria was funny, Mini our driver was also fun. Both were very informative .
It was showing when we were there so made the day even more special
Gloria also gave us other tips around Barcelona like places to eat etc
Overall was a beautiful day and didn't feel like a long day at all. Definitely recommend this tour!

What an amazingly trip!
Martha super knowledgeable guide with a delightful personality
Pedro our captain drove us back and forth safely through the narrow roads and foggy weather
The history lesson from Martha spiced up with a salt of politics made my day!
Martha you made a long 12 hours ride seems like a picnic and for that I give you the super guide 5 stars ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️
Definitely I recommend the trip if you’re a nature/history lover.
I only wished they had wifi on the bus other than that I will change NOTHING 👌👍
It was a good trip, and Camilo was great, but the village in France was okay. I would have rather had more time to spend in Andorra

This involves a lot of sitting on a bus, but...I don’t know of another way to see these gorgeous mountains and the small country of Andorra unless you drive yourself. We really enjoyed the stunning Mountain View’s and the picturesque towns we stoped at. The guide was very informative also.

We traveled during the Tsunami in Barcelona which will explain the end of this review.

Javier, our guide, and Mickey, our driver, were gifted in their respective roles.

We loved the journey to Andorra. The only thing we wanted was to see more of old Andorra. Too much shopping emphasis, but it was a fantastic trip. The Pyrenees are beautiful mountains, and we were thankful for so much beauty. The Catalan town was a refreshing change from the cities we normally visit.

Our return trip had altered route due to marches and police closing roads. It resulted in Javier and Mickey finding a route back to the city which Javier (a lifelong Barcelona resident) had never used. When we reached the city limits, the road was closed, so Javier walked us a short distance to the Metro. He safely returned us to our destinations with cheerful encouragement. No, you don’t need a ticket to exit at Maria Christina. But thanks for giving us the security of one.

Very pleasant tour guide- informative, professional, knowledgable & personable.
Beautiful places to visit, lovely scenery. Didn't personally like the capital of Andorra but still pleased we have seen it. A long day but plenty of stops on the way. Great to have seen different parts of Europe and get out of Barcelona for a day.

I am a Japanese tourist and joined the tour by myself.
The tour was much better than I thought. We went to a small town, Baga, before crossing the French boarder to go to Ax-les-Thermes. I wouldn't have had the opportunity to visit such small towns if I did not join the tour. The visit to Andola was also interesting. I thought Andorra la Vella, the capital of Andorra, is just a rural town, since there is no airport, no train stations, etc. But this was a modern city.

The tour guide, Martha and the driver were perfect!
Martha explained us everything we need including history of Catalunya and Andorra. The driver stopped at a few nice view spots in order to let us take pictures of Pyrenees and Andorra.
I would recommend taking the tour for everybody who can understand English.

What a complete waste of time. Spent the day in the bus. 30 minutes first stop 45 minutes in second stop and 70 minutes third stop. We gobbled down our lunch to stay in the time frame. 12 hour tour but 91/2 are in the bus. Take out the first stop and it will us more time at the others. Not happy

We only stayed in Barcelona for 4 days, this tour is excellent especially you do not have much time or you don't drive. Tour guide is super friendly and helpful! We had delicious lunch in France and about an hour free time in Andorra. I recommend this tour to everyone!

We really enjoyed this trip! The tour guide was great full of information, double checked all times to be back and made the effort with everyone! and the driver was brilliant driving very safe& patient. Fully air conned mini bus too!

I would recommend doing this trip as you see a lot and have plenty of time to see where you are! Andorra is really nice, as is France but with Andorra you really see the country side and lovely villages!

Well worth the travel and money!

This tour was great, and our tour guide Pablo made the tour even better. The bus wasn't overly crowded, and you could see all of the scenery just fine from the back of the bus. I only wish we would have had more time in France and Andorra. Because we knew there was a time limit, we just grabbed a quick sandwich in France so we could eat while walking around. If we would have gone to a restaurant in either place, then we would have spent our whole time there.

Tour started at 7 am and we returned (not to the same location) at 7:15 pm. I was surprised the tour did not offer bottled water for the bus ride. Most of the 12 hours was spent on the bus; no bathroom on the bus. The 3 stops (Spain, France, Andorra) were quite brief, we had an hour or so at each stop. I didn't realize we would be spending approximately 9 hours on the bus, as I didn't calculate the distances. The guide did give us a lot of information. A tiring day.

Xavier was an engaged, knowledgeable, and witty tour leader, who kept the group on schedule and provided excellent commentary regarding history, cuisine, culture, and customs. The bus was comfortable, and the rule allowing regular change of seating made the trip seem less lengthy and welcoming. The starting point is easy to locate near the city center.

A good trip into the Pyrenees Mountains. First stop Baga, in a quaint medievil town in Spain. We were able to purchase pastries from the bakery and hot chocolate from the pub for breakfast. Then onto Ax Les-Thermes in France. We had time to wander around this sleepy village and dip our feet into the open air thermal waters. The hot springs were very hot. Some from the group had lunch here and enjoyed the food. Then onto Andorra. We stopped at a couple of places to breath in the fresh mountain air and take some photos before going into Andorra La Vella. There was really only time to shop or sit down to lunch. We chose the lunch option and found a lovely cafe behind the pedestrian street. I did still manage to find some souveniers. The guide was very cheery and told some great tales. A great day.
I took this tour not knowing what to expect. And trust me, it did not disappoint. Our guide was Enrique and he was very knowledgeable, funny and extremely helpful. Would recommend it to everyone.

This was an extensive 12+hr journey from northern Spain to Andorra. We enjoyed the little cities tucked into mountains, the stops along the highway to take in the scenery and grab some pictures, and the knowledge of our tour guide as she told us stories about the locations we visited. We were pretty exhausted by the end of the day, but it was well worth it. One especially memorable aspect of this trip was getting to visit less touristy but equally compelling destinations. It made it very memorable!

We had an amazing day trip! Sergio was an amazing tour guide! He was very knowledgeable about the areas that we visited. Sergio ensured we all were aware of when the next restroom breaks would occur. He was friendly and had a good sense of humor. He took great care to ensure everyone was having a good time. Near the end of the trip Sergio also spoke to each person to find out if they had additional questions or needed recommendations for dinner. Highly recommend this tour with Sergio! Also appreciated the bus driver getting us to each destination safely. Date of visit July 16, 2019.

Had an amazing time on this tour, it felt organised and professional and Jordi knew his stuff! The rest of the tour group was super friendly and interactive which all in all resulted in a fantastic trip to three beautiful countries and memories to remember for a lifetime!
Good plan... Probably stay at Andorra can be increased ... Professional service no complaints really

My 15 & 18 yr olds LOVED this trip. Our guide, Sergio was OUTSTANDING. Entertaining, knowledgable and committed to ensuring we enjoyed ourselves and learned a lot about the region. Driver M was also safe and courteous Re: some of the comments. It IS a long day and you are on a group tour covering a lot of ground so you may feel rushed at some points. If you like to explore everything at your leisure, this trip is NOT for you. If you want to purchase something specific in Andorra, have a plan b4 u go bc there is not a lot of time. We loved it and would take another tour with Sergio wherever....he was that good! He was generous w/overall recommendations in Barcelona and we followed each and were not disappionted.

We took a couple extra days at the end of our lengthy trip to Spain and I always wanted to see the Pyrenees Mountains. The sights and sounds of our worlwind tour of Spain was nothing short of magnificent, but there was something I wanted to see, the natural beauty of the boarder between Spain and France. The photographs of this area on Google had drawn me into locating Trip Advisor and this wonderful tour. Our tour guide was a beautiful knowledgable woman and the combination of the small passenger van made it feel like a friend taking us on a private site seeing tour. The 12 hour excursion seemed to go by very quickly as every moment was filled with beautiful scenery, great stops including snow covered mountain tops and the sweet country Andorra. I recommend this trip to anyone who visits Barcelona.

There’s no other way to describe this tour other than AMAZING!! It’s well worth the money. It is an all day trip but it’s worth the time. Arnold was our tour guide and he was nothing short of great. Our bus driver and even great. Pictures just don’t do this tour justice.

Such a great tour, Gloria was our guide and she was excellent, great sense of humour, explained everything really well and kept us on track throughout the day. We enjoyed the different cultures and the scenery was amazing. I would highly recommend this tour if you're visiting Barcelona.

A great deal to see beautiful countrysides of three countries. I didn’t feel like rushing into moving on to the next thing. Had enough time to enjoy the view and take photos! Laura was a tour guide on the day and she was very knowledgeable and approachable :) Overall, I would recommend this tour.

I was skeptical reading the reviews. I can see the trip easily spiral if there are technical problems or people challenges. My wife and I are seasoned business and personal travelers and enjoy learning about the local culture, foods, sights, and sounds. We found tremendous value during our trip. We got a chance to speak French, and put our feet in the hot spring, learned about Andorra, a country neither one of us knew about, and enjoyed being out of Barcelona Spain. Overall, we really enjoyed the experience. Further, the tour guide Jordi was very good.

This tour was a great way to see three countries, including one we wouldn't have otherwise gotten to. It was well-organized (clean bus, on time, etc.) and our guide was great. It was so fun it didn't feel like 12 hours.

There are various reviews around the trip to Andorra and would agree that it's not the destination that's worth going - nothing more than a place to buy cheap cigarettes, perfume, liquor and chocolates. The trip was much more interesting, thanks to an irreverent guide named Sergio. Fantastic job overall.

We stopped in Baga, which was a good stop for a few photos in an old town. Grab a coffee and a toilet break and you're off. We couldn't go to Aix because of the weather so we were bundled to Bourg-Madame. This was the highlight of the tour I think.

We stopped by the old church, enjoyed the snow, and had some cheese and cured meats. The company sponsored these as we missed out on going to Aix. Well worth the side trip. I wish we stayed longer and bought some cheeses back with us.

Next was Andorra, which is sadly nothing more than a long shopping strip. No one also told us that siestas were observed so most shops were closed. Good thing we had a good lunch at a restaurant called 120. More on that on a separate review.

After 2 hours we drove back to Barcelona. Had a stop in between for drinks - courtesy of the tour company. Nice way to end the tour.

My only beef is that the bus badly needed its shocks replaced. It wasn't the most comfortable ride. Tony was a good driver, but boy did he drive like his bus like a taxi.

Sergio was a consummate professional, and one of the better tour guides I've had thus far. Would recommend going to this tour - at least once in your lifetime.

Alfons - drove very safely
Matteus - was friendly and very informative guide
The tour was well planned: when to use the bathroom, eat and drinks and photo opportunities
5 stops in total: Baga, Spain - Ax Les Thermes, France - Andorra's peak point - Vella, Andorra and Bar Restaurant Can Valls, Spain (for free drinks)
The ride to Andorra was breathtaking with all the snow covered views of the Pyreenes...
Overall it was worth every cent experience !

It was nice to go and visit Andorra, thats all, very long trip in bus, small stop in a french town. Its better to do only Andorra and spend more time there. Little expensive for what it is. I could rent a car and go directly to Andorra instead. Average tour. Guide tour Aniar was good though, he did a good job

We did the 3 countries in 1 day with Feli (guide) and Tony (driver) both of whom made the journey enjoyable and comfortable. Yes, you are on the bus early and for a while but how else are you expected to cover three countries in one day? The tour is well planned and Feli made sure to point out bathrooms along the way. Our first stop was in Baga where Feli did a mini walking tour and told stories about the town's history. Then, we stopped at Ax Les Thermes and dipped our feet in the hot springs. We got off at some picture spots, got our passport stamped in Andorra and even did some duty free shopping there.

If you do decide to take this tour, I strongly recommend getting an overview of how much time is spent at each location so you can plan meals accordingly. If I could change anything I wish we could have brought back sandwiches or snacks to eat on the bus. It would have allowed more time to explore in the cities. Especially since we only had 1 hour and 15 mins to spend in Andorra! If I could do it all over again, I would have eaten at Ax Les Thermes so we could have spent more time walking around Andorra instead of finding a spot to eat, ordering and eating.

On the way back, Feli gave out personalized recommendations based on what he learned about each group. I would gladly go on another tour with him any day!

Had the pleasure of joining the 3 countries in one day with Feliciano (guide) and Tony (driver). The day consists of a significant amount of driving, but is well planned so that you are only in the car for relatively short periods of time. The beautiful scenery and interesting information from Feliciano served as a good distraction. A highlight for me was visiting Ax-Les Thermes and driving through/visiting Andorra. I was very delighted to stumble upon a Dalí sculpture in Andorra la Vella. I highly recommend this tour! Feliciano and Tony did an excellent job.

Overall pretty a amazing day. A little minus for me was how the seats were tight for my legs. We went to Ax les Thermes instead og Mont Louis as detailed in the description. Don't think it matters much because Ax was very nice. But details should be right. Minor flaw. A propos: Good guide and driver.

It was a very long ride in a relatively small coach with cramped seats. Most stops seemed rushed, and in Andorra, we did not even have enough time to finish our meal before we had to literally run to catch the coach for our ride back to Barcelona. The tour guide was above average but not memorable.

Our guide Miguel was great, very knowledgeable and accommodating. The destinations were awesome -- with great views, lots of shops and quaint towns! HOWEVER, the bus leaves around 7AM and you're back at around 7PM (depending on traffic) - this wasn't the issue. The issue was, you're on the bus for at least 60% of the time - that's 7 hours on the bus. Due to limited time and distance from place to place, you're not able to enjoy as much. Definitely not worth ~$150 per person, not even half the cost, unfortunately.

1. First bus broke down before getting out of Barcelona. 2. Second bus was approx 85 to 90 degrees as air conditioning did not work. $600 for four to sweat for 12 hours. 3. Microphone in bus did not work so could only hear every 10th word of guide. 4. Poor English of guide so could barely understand what I did hear. 5. Visits to stops cut short because bus driver said he had a contract and would not go over time to make up for the near 2 hour delay getting new bus. Paid 600 dollars for a miserable hot bus ride with basically no guide experience. I would have demanded my money back but office was closed when we got out of the sauna bus.

We were planning on going to Barcelona for 5 days and my daughter wanted to visit as many countries as we could so we decided to book this tour. From the start, it was a wonderful experience! Our guide, Maria, was so friendly and knowledgable. I enjoyed hearing the history of the different countries and how they were all intertwined. The views from the bus were spectacular and seeing the smaller viliages/towns helped me appreciate the true history of the area. It is a great day trip for those who want to see more of Spain than just the city and for those who want to see a bit of France and Andorra (when will you ever get the chance to do that?)

Of note, I left my phone on the bus and the staff (Claudia and Maria) were so kind and went out of their way to return it to me. I have been on another tour in Barcelona with a different company but Explore Catalunya was definitely a step above the rest. I would definitely book with them again!

This tour exceeded my expectations. Our tour guide, Camilo (Cam), was everything you want a guide to be—friendly, enthusiastic, extremely knowledgeable, full of cheesy jokes. The scenery was absolutely beautiful. The tour ran a solid 12 hours from departure to arrival back in Barcelona, and most of that was driving—so it's a tiring day, but the views are spectacular. You get ~1.5 hours time on your own in both Ax-Les-Thermes, France and Andorra la Vella, Andorra. Great way to experience a broad swath of countryside (and countries).

Our tour guide Matias was knowlegeable and the locations we stopped at were great. Matias gave an interesting coverage of the history of Baga and Ax-les-Thermes. It was amazing driving through the Pyrennes. Unfortunately the bus was so uncomfortable. The seats were narrow and ther was insufficient leg room. We could not hear the commentry on ther return journey due to the noise of the bus.
Al of these issues caused a lot of stress for a large proportion of the bus and made the trip feel even longer. We did arrive back to Barcelona moe than 1 hour late which impacted our evening plans. The issues with the bus impacted heavily on the enjoyment of our trip.

This tour was amazing! Joseph was our tour guide, and he was very knowledgeable about all our stops. He was very passionate, hospitable, and high-energy!
