The coolest stop was the picture perfect location where one can see France, Spain, and Andorra all from the same mountain top. The view was breathtaking! Bring a camera and good walking shoes.

Be prepared for a very long day - but we loved it! The guide was great, pointing out things to see as we drove. The scenery was spectacular, just breathtaking. Most of the time is spent in a bus, going from place to place. Andorra was somewhat disappointing - the area is gorgeous but the stop was in a supermarket parking lot of the capital to visit a mall. I loved hearing about all the history of the region. The tour is 11 hours long - so we got back to Barcelona at rush hour - finding a taxi to get us back to our hotel was difficult, especially since we were pretty tired.
Our guide Gloria did an amazing job keeping us informed about where we were and it's history and fun facts. The driver Petro was an excellent driver and kept us to time
We enjoyed this tour. The passionate guidance by Carlos who had many tips on what to do made this a great day. When visiting Andorra it is really worth it to visit the old part of the city.
Had a fabulous day visiting Andorra and seeing bit of Spain and France. Beautiful scenery, spectacular views and our guide Arnold was superb. Would definitely recommend.
12 hours seems like a a lot but it’s a great way to just see the countryside and little towns you never knew existed. 10/10
We took off late, arrived early, sat for 40 minutes in the middle of nowhere, then waited a further 20 minutes for a bus. Never again
Good experience for travellers who have not seen snow before and cheap duty free goods in Andorra (tobacco, liquor/wine, cosmetic & perfume)
Will do it again. Miguel and Nikki were awesome! They brought us to nice places and made the 13 our trip enjoying and interesting. Worth the money!

Due to epiphany day the tour was scheduled in a different order, but the guide Camilo made sure we got enough time at each village to explore. The roadside photostops,told stories and overall plesant vibe of the guide added up to a great day out of bussy Barcelona.
It would have been so much better to stop at the old town area of Andorra rather at the modern shopping mall. Can do that at home. The other stops were good.

If you have an additional day after exploring Barcelona, this is a fun trip. You get a good sense of the countryside, the magnificent Pyrenees, three distinct cultures, and the history behind those cultures. For me, an attraction as good as the three cities we visited was our guide, Gloria. She was knowledgeable, personable, enthusiastic, and funny. It wasn’t long into the trip that she knew everyone’s name and our special interests, which she made sure to satisfy.

My husband and I were really glad that we did this tour. The sun was rising as we were driving past Montserrat and that was just the beginning of the amazing scenery that we enjoyed that day. Our tour guide Enrique gave us good historical and cultural information and also had a great sense of humor. We had a little scare with a warning light in the bus coming on but the appropriate steps were taken and we made it safely back to Barcelona without a problem. It was a day well spent.

long trip, 30 minute to walk around food market, not worth a 12 hour trip and waste of money, the bus was completely full and too small and tight for this type of long trip.
we only had 45 minutes in Andora and to do what?

Thanks to our guide Gloria.She is amazing. We learned a lot of interesting about Catalynia`s history & culture.She was very helpful and she took care about everything we need.Thank you Gloria! Overall the trip is worth to be in despite the fact that there is nothing interesting in the small French town-just waste your time. Steve. 09-20-2019
Very well organised tour. The tour guide Sirgio is funny and speak very good English. He explained everything very well and happy for us to ask as many questions.

This was a great tour. It started at 07h00 in the morning with Miguel as our tour guide. I was impress with all the information he gave us on our way to Baga. Although we had rainy weather in Baga and Ax-Les-Thermes, we still had a great time. When we reached Andorra the sun was shining again and we could enjoy our shopping. On our way home we enjoyed the spectacular views of the Pyrenees. It is a tiring trip of 8hours, but with the beautiful views definitely worth it. Miguel was excellent!

Over the past week we decided to go a little over board and booked 8 separate excursions. By far the best experience was with Sergio whose charming personality, experience, and personal attentiveness made the day memorable. Regardless of the tour you book, Sergio will take it to the next level. Looking forward to our next visit.
Thanks..

We had the absolute pleasure of having Sergio as our guide. He was incredibly attentive, super personable, very informative, a joy to spend the day with. We felt his heart and passion of his native country. Be prepare to see some of the most beautiful sites the three three countries have to offer. Nature at its best. Pic is of us in the thermal springs in France.

HIGHLY recommended as part of the Barcelona experience
Trip was excellent. Even though a big trip for anyone. Thank you to Tony & Alex. May have been a bit tough on elderly and infirm but would recommend it. From Aussies Gerard & Merise
our tour guide Martha was excellent very knowledgeable and friendly, we love the little cities in Andorra and france.

Very well explain by our tour guide,Gloria. Beautiful sceneries and confortable bus. The meeting point by the Palau de la music was very easy to find. We had an excellent time, Andorra was beautiful, the night before it snowed so the view was breathtaking. We had an amazing time at the little town in France. Love the whole trip, and I would recommend it.

Our guide, Gloria, and our driver, Tony were fantastic. It's a long day, but so worth it. Gloria was VERY knowledgable, spoke great English and was just fun to be with.

Highly recommended!

I went on this trip on the 12th of June and had a lovely time. Our guide Lorea was very knowledgeable, friendly and made sure we enjoyed ourselves. It was an early start so a few of us were quite sleepy at times but she made sure to wake us up at the points where the scenery was the best, which I really appreciated as I was worried I might miss some good sights from dozing too much (lol).
Also, the places we visited were lovely and the views were stunning. It is alot of time on the coach but it's broken up into enough sections that it wasnt much of an issue.
Very rare to find a tour spanning so many languages and cultures. The pace was great with many opportunities to stop along the way. Xavier was extremely personable and upbeat.

We had Jordi for our tour guide. He was so friendly, knowledgeable, and personable! I truly loved the whole day. There is a lot of time spent in the car, but there is a great balance of nature, history, and culture in the places that you visit to make the day worthwhile!! They pretty much break everything up in 1.5 hour increments, so it’s usually 1.5 hours driving, 1.5 hours in a town, 1.5 hours driving, etc. Honestly, I loved it. I would highly recommend it—it was a great break from the hustle and bustle of Barcelona!! I learned so much and loved being able to enjoy the mountain views.

We went on this tour on 29 May 2019. Xavier, our guide was great value - friendly, helpful (including about what to and not to buy in Andorra) and knowledgeable. The driver (sorry forgotten his name) gave us a very smooth ride over windy mountain roads.

I particularly liked that we went to non-touristy villages both in Spain and in France. It was nice to see ordinary places as well as the wonderful Pyrenees mountains and valleys.

First we were hesitant about this tour: it seemed overwhelmingly long, plus we were discouraged by other tour guides who didn’t offer it. We decided to go anyway: what a great idea! We really enjoyed it. It was well organized: the departure was on time, there was a good combination of sitting on the bus and walking, and Laura the tour guide was absolutely amazing which contributed to our experience a great deal! Besides being very knowledgeable and professional, she was also very personable, funny and sweet. She loved her job and genuinely cared about all visitors to get the best experience. Tony’s driving skills were also admirable: he navigated a big bus thru very narrow windy roads high up in the mountains with great confidence. Hats off! Overall we had a wonderful experience and would highly recommend it to all, as long as you get Laura as your guide (we heard different comments about other guides). To those who complain about a very short time at every stop we can tell, they should have expected it if they planned to visit 3 countries in 1 day!
Tripadvisor wouldnt allow me to post more than one picture: Laura is standing on the left:).

We enjoyed being part of Gloria's "people" on this tour. She is an amazing tour guide with a wealth of knowledge that she shared during the tour. The driver, Tony, did a great job driving us. Personally, I would have preferred more time in France and Baga than in Andorra. Gloria did a fantastic job explaining the history and culture of the areas we visited and the area we travelled through. A great tour during our visit to Barcelona!

The trip is a long day but has 4 stops that makes the day not to seem to long. The first stop Baga I found the most interesting with Laura, our guide, giving a very good history
of town and Catalona in general. Then in to France in a town with a hot springs. I kind of felt the stop was so you could say you were in France. Next to Andorra where the countryside is beautiful with snow when I was there but the town we stopped in was mostly just high end shopping and not something quaint which I was hoping for. Then back to Barcelona with a stop for a drink to break up the trip back. The commentary by our guide is what made it worth while.

The tour guide was fine, this is nothing against him. However, I would not recommend this tour. It’s a long day, you are in the van for most of it. Stop number one we had 15 minutes of our own time, stop number two we had about 45 minutes? But there was nothing to do there. Both of the first two stops seemed like a ghost town. The third stop seemed more lively and I believe we had about an hour but it was just enough time to grab lunch and not really explore. The views while on the van were very beautiful, but again, not worth $150 in my opinion.

Our bus left promptly at 07:02 with our guide Jordi keeping us interested and awake ☺ with all sorts of fun facts. The day was very hectic and exhausting but well worth it. Keep in mind that Andorra is located at 2,400 meters and the temperature there is much lower than in Barcelona. We had 4 degrees C and light snow as we approached. There isn't much to do in Andorra besides enjoying the view and of course amazing Duty Free shopping. I'm not referring to the big store labeled "Duty Free" because it only had alcohol, cigarettes, perfume and chocolates. All the stores seem to have really good prices. Remember to dress well. Ax Les Thermes is also a cute little town. There was some sort of a farmer's market there to buy ready food etc. We had the best hot chocolate there in one little cafe. and of course there are the hot springs which are very hot so no one could actually do more than just dip their feet inside. Do remember good walking shoes and dress warm. I would have liked to have spent longer in Andorra and France and felt a bit rushed. I guess that is what its like when you need to squeeze 3 countries into 1 day. I would suggest doing a 2 country tour with just Andorra and France and dropping the Spanish bit as ut felt like a waste of time to us.
Jordi - you came accross as really dedicated to your job, giving us all the relevant information and making it fascinating and interesting - so much so that we didn't even fall asleep on the bus on the way back from Barcelona.

I'd been fascinated with the idea of visiting Andorra, and this seemed like the best way to do it. That being said, be aware you're going to be spending most of the time driving. It's almost all driving. But the views are amazing, and only the return portion back into Barcelona is a little dull. Baga was a quaint, beautiful little town, but the visit there is very brief. Our guide Jordi was great, and told us we could buy coffee, but they wound up taking forever and he scolded us for ordering it at all.

Ax-les-Thermes wasn't anything special. If I had to guess, I'd say it was just the closest town of note near the route to Andorra. More time here than Baga, but not enough to do anything.

Andorra was gorgeous, and worth a visit for how unique it is. I wish Jordi had told us more about the country's history though. Still, we had enough time here to walk around some, shop if you wanted, and grab some quick food.

Then back on the bus and back to Barcelona.

So yeah, just a ton of driving with quick glimpses of three towns. I was totally expecting this though, so it met my expectations. The roads there are a tad daunting (and are toll roads), so renting a car may be too much. There is a bus you can take to Andorra from Barcelona, but I'd only recommend that if you'd like to spend a day or two there.

This was a very interesting day where we learned a lot about the history in Catalonia, France, Spain and Andorra. Miguel was our tour guide and he was an excellent tour guide. Mickey was our driver and he gave us a smooth and conformable ride.
We highly recommend this tour.

The mountains were covered in snow when we went and it was breathtaking! Baga Spain is the first stop, cute little medeviel town. Little town in France is next, again nice quaint French town with a hot spring. Andorra is last, and I have to say, the most disappointing. The little country itself is nice, but the stop is in the capitol city and it’s just a long shopping street, nothing special at all. The best thing about it was Dali’s dripping clock sculpture. I wish these tours didn’t focus on shopping so much, there’s plenty of that in Barcelona. However, our guide Xavier, was very good, nice and full of all kinds of knowledge! And kudos to these bus drivers getting us all there and back safely! Over all an interesting excursion, but a lot of time on the bus.

We loved our experience on this tour! We saw so much for one day and our guide, Feliciano, was very helpful! There was a lot of time spent on the bus, but the views made the long rides well worth it. Our guide had lots of helpful information to share and made our experience even better! Would definitely recommend this trip!

My sister and I did the three countries in a day trip with Miguel (guide). He was awesome- funny, knowledgable, and kept us all on track. The bus seats were very narrow, so beware if you're at all obese! Other than the views heading into Andorra, that stop was just for shopping. Worth it for a passport stamp though, and the stops in Spain and France were amazing!
I really enjoyed the tour, it was a long but interesting trip, not only the final destinations, but the road is beautiful. The explanations of Nicolau enriches the experience.
We had an amazing tour on August 30th with Gloria and Victor! Great information and beautiful scenery! Thank you Gloria for a fun day!

We had an awesome trip with guide Gloria and driver Victor.

They both did a great job of entertaining and informing us of the areas we traveled through on this trip. Both did an exceptional job.

Beautiful areas of Spain, France and Andorra to travel through and learn a great deal about the history of the area.

Thanks for a fun day.

This trip was wonderful and fun but long. If you can't walk up long, steep flights of stairs be warned that in Baga you will be required too. Also in Andorra there is a steep climb. We opted to sit the last one out but in Baga there is no other way back to the bus. When they say moderate amount of walking they are vastly underestimating it.

That being said our guide, Lorna was excellent. She was informative and fun and kept us laughing. She made a point of coming around and talking to everyone and getting to know you a bit. We stopped on the way back to Barcelona and had our first taste of Cava which was wonderful. It was a wonderful, if long and tiring, day. But how often do you get the chance to see three countries in one day? Definitely worth a day.

We traveled with a walker (push style) for mobility issue, and this trip was quite suitable.

Great way to see the Pyrenees and Andorra from Barcelona.

The stops in Spain were great the tour of Axe Le Themes was nice but very rushed.

Main draw back on this tour was no food allowed to be eatten on the bus. This tour has a very early start time and the first stop is 1.5 hours into the trip.

Quick stop at petrol station for toilet stop & yes back on the bus.
Disappointing with the trip, not helped by those being late back. We discussed hiring a car and so wished we had of done. There was no time to do anything and really didn’t want to go to Andorra just to look at shops which I could do at home

I had a lot of fun with great weather. It could not have more perfect. It was supposed to rain and it did. It only rained for 20 min ridiculously and then nice again. Only at the end. Laura was fantastic and organized. 5 star service!

we visited the little town Baga in Spain to start our tour, it was lovely, getting away from the busy big smoke, people were lovely and friendly, a lot of photo opportunities. I enjoyed France as well, but not so much Andorra, we had an hour free time in Andorra but we were dropped off at a supermarket parking lot, the guide suggested to shop in the nearby shopping centre to buy cheap booze, not everyone's a drinker. the view of the snowy mountains of Andorra was great though, and got a stamp on the passport, so that's Andorra! i found the customs in Andorra was quite easy-peasy, our guide collected our passport to get it stamped, so the custom didnt even see our face in person...

Seeing a herd of cows running through the streets of Baga and the great tour guide and driver team of Gloria and Franklin

The tour was great with the ability to see a lot of places. It was best for the end of the trip because of the amount of time.

Here a piece of advise, based on true life experience: if you plan to rent a car in a foreign country, avoid AVIS.
Here is what happened to us: we rented a car in Rome at the Fiumicino airport. While driving on highway, we experienced a flat tire. First major issue: the car did not have a jack. With help of passers-by, we borrowed a jack from another car. Then came the second major issue: the wheel was completely frozen in place, and was impossible to detach from the axel. We tried very hard, even with the help of a 8-feet long lever, but could not take the flat tire out. And then came the third issue: we called AVIS Roadside Assistance, four times over one hour, left messages, but got no answer, nor anyone ever called us back. Eventually, we called the police, who very promptly send a tow track. The repair shop they brought us to managed (with extreme brute force) to detach and change the flat tire; their diagnosis: wheels were never rotated, for at least 50,000 miles. We were back on our way, three hours and 200 Euros later.
Subsequent complain with Customer Care (both in Itay as well as in the US) did not even brought an apology or an offer of compensation.
My complain: lack of proper equipment, lack of proper care of the car, and lack of assistance.
Thanks God we speak Italian, otherwise this might have turned in a much longer and much more expensive ordeal

Three Countries in One Day: France, Andorra, Spain: Yes, it can be achieved! Sergio wants to ensure that all his charges have a wonderful time. We enjoyed our day with our guide, Adrian. He was a great driver, very knowledgeable, and gave interesting descriptions along the way. We stopped several times to take pictures and enjoy the scenery. For us the visit to the hot springs in France was fun but Andorra was a little disappointing as it's more for shopping. But to see more of the general area and the beauty of the Pyrenees, this was a great excursion, as long as you like long car rides.
This whole trip was filled with beautiful vistas and even though there was a lot of riding in a bus the views were worth it. We enjoyed each of our stops and our guide was delightful.

This tour was spectacular. This was the highlight of our trip to Barcelona. Our tour guide was amazing, he was very knowledgeable. Highly recommended!

We booked this trip to take advantage of the opportunity to see some more of the countryside as well as the additional cities and countries listed in the itinerary. It turned out to be one of our highlights of our time in Spain. Our tour guide was Miguel, and, as many have mentioned, he was an incredible guide with a wealth of knowledge and energy. From the outset, he set the tone for a great time. It is a lot of traveling, but we did not feel rushed and Miguel did a great job of pacing the trip and talking points. We would definitely book with Explore Catalunya again.

Gloria was our tour guide, and even though she usually doesn’t do this tour, you wouldn’t have known if she hadn’t said it. She was great and made the tour very interesting. I agree with some other reviewers that more stopping and no shopping would have been better, with more time off the bus. But still it was great.

We took this tour on February 15, 2019. It was a crystal clear day and the scenery was amazing. Ana was our tour guide and could have not been more delightful. She has a super sweet personality and a very pleasant voice. Our bus driver (forgive me for not remembering his name) was also great. Be advised that if you take this tour at this time of the year, the weather is very cold in the mountains. Dress appropriately in order to enjoy all the aspects. We did not have the proper clothing with us but were still able to stay warm by enjoying a few more coffees inside away from the cold. The stops were well timed and there was no wasted motion. We departed and arrived back in Barcelona as scheduled, thanks to the traffic conditions and other tour guests being punctual on their returns to the bus. We highly recommend this tour if you are short on time and want to squeeze in as much of Spain, France, and Andorra as possible. Thank you Explore Catalunya!

We were lucky that the weather was so beautiful. The tour was exactly as described, a way to see 3 countries in one day. Andorra was stunning! Our tour guide gave nice short tours in both Baga and Ax Les Thermes, and fantastic recommendations for lunch and shopping. We enjoyed the day, and our guide was great!
The trip in itself was spectacular; however, the tour guide made it memorable with his knowledge and sense of humor. Thoroughly enjoyed it.

Sergio, our guide, was excellent. He told us about everything you can think of (History, geography, current Catalonian politics...) he also offered up advice for going out to dinner after the Tour. Sergio and our bus driver were very accommodating with our three-year-old daughter. They let us use a booster seat and helped us with the stroller on multiple occasions. The places we visited were very nice. However, we would’ve rather spent more time in each place and just come back later in the evening. All in all, it was a great way to visit a lot of places in a short amount of time and with a wonderful tour guide and a great driver.

We learned so much with it guide, Cam, who have us great information and advice on places to eat as well! Definitely 5 stars for the guide! The driving was not as excellent but he was very accommodating as well. I went with family and didn't expect to enjoy it as much as I did. It added a lot to my experience and education about the area and its roots.

My friends and I had 6 days in Barcelona and decided to get out of the city and go for the a day tour. I enjoyed the scenic bus ride more than destinations and I think it's a good way spend a day especially we had an intense walking tour the day before in Barcelona.
Excellent Visit . Had fun !!! Visiting the village in Pyrenees and the snow capped mountains of Andorra was an out of world experience.

The trip had great views of the Pyrenees mountains. Our first stop was Baga which was pretty little village with some wonderful architecture. We did not make it to Ax Les Thermes due to an avalanche blocked the roads. Instead, they treated the group to a drink and a snack at a French cafe before going to Andorra. The guide and the driver were great and did the best they could to supplement Ax Les Thermes .
Our guide Xavi was really nice and knowledgeable. The views are amazing. There is a bunch of driving time but I didn't really feel it because it's broken up with breaks nicely.
